title: Estates Maintenance Officer
description:
Please note that there is some flexibility in terms of hours for this position.

Job Title - Estates Maintenance Officer

About You

Are you looking to make a hands-on, positive impact in a supportive school community? Do you bring genuine enthusiasm for working in an educational environment where your daily efforts directly benefit our students?

Whether you are an experienced tradesperson, a skilled maintenance professional, or someone with strong practical aptitude eager to learn and grow, we want to hear from you. We are looking for someone who takes deep pride in keeping our facilities running safely, smoothly, and sustainably.

If you want to join an organisation where Estates staff are recognised as essential partners in our success, where your growth is backed by funded formal apprenticeship qualifications, and where staff are always treated people first, this is the place for you.


The Role

As an Estates Maintenance Officer, you will join a dedicated site and support team at The Oxford Academy, playing a pivotal role in creating a safe, clean, and inspiring environment where our students can thrive every day.

We are open to applications from individuals with varying levels of experience:

  • Experienced Candidates: You bring established skills in site management, health and safety compliance, practical DIY, or building maintenance trades.

  • Less Experienced Candidates: You bring a strong practical mindset, a proactive attitude, and the enthusiasm to develop your craft through structured support and CPLD pathways..

Why This Role Matters

At The Oxford Academy, our Estates team does far more than maintain buildings - you help shape the physical heartbeat of our school. By keeping our grounds safe, welcoming, and well-cared for, you directly enable high-quality learning and help foster a sense of pride across our entire community. We genuinely value this role as a cornerstone of our day-to-day success.


Why Join Us

This is an important time to join The Oxford Academy, where our values of ‘commitment to others, commitment to learning’ drive everything we do. We are seeking a skilled individual who shares our deep belief that education has the power to transform lives, communities, and society for the better.

You will be joining a team where staff are genuinely proud of the work they do, recognising how valuable a high-quality education is for improving pupils' life chances, and remain very positive about working at the school (Ofsted 2026).

At The Oxford Academy, support staff are valued as essential professional partners in our school's success. We actively invest in our team through CPLD and formal apprenticeship pathways funded via the River Learning Trust Apprenticeship Levy. Whether you are starting out or looking to broaden your career, our support staff have successfully completed Level 3 to Level 5 qualifications, enabling meaningful internal career progression.

Shaping Futures and Long-Term Success

Continued Professional Development

‘With the Trust's support and the Apprenticeship Levy, I completed both a Level 5 Operations Management apprenticeship and a Level 5 CIPD qualification. That structured CPLD provided the foundation to move into HR; a shift made possible by RLT’s commitment to internal professional development’ (Manager, The Oxford Academy).

Community and Connection

‘I am delighted to have joined TOA. I have felt consistently supported by my line manager, Nora Ward, as well as the Senior Leadership, Central teams and HR colleagues. From day one, it was clear that this is an environment where I can build effective systems, grow professionally, and see the real-world impact of my work. It’s a privilege to be part of a community that truly lives its values; placing students at the heart of everything while ensuring staff feel respected and genuinely valued’ (Manager, The Oxford Academy).

‘The atmosphere at The Oxford Academy is truly like no other, it is a space that is as inspiring as it is motivating. There is an infectious energy here driven by a staff and students that fills me with pride. I’ve reached a point where I feel like a stick of rock, I am TOA through and through’ (Senior Leader, The Oxford Academy).

Care and Compassion

‘What I didn't expect, though, was to find an environment where the differing strengths of each and every staff member are valued and that time would be invested in me to be the best I could be. I ventured through a number of roles and, since I retired from teaching, I have continued in a support role that enables me to make a difference.

One other thing that should be highlighted is that staff are thought of as people, and not work units. I suffered a bout of serious ill-health and the TOA family supported me in my return to the chalkface, and I will be forever grateful to them’ (Administrator, The Oxford Academy).

‘Being part of creating successful futures for so many students is something that I will always be proud of. My enthusiasm grows for my job every single day’ (Intervention Tutor, The Oxford Academy).

Flexibility

While this position is advertised as full time, we warmly consider requests for part-time hours or flexible working arrangements. Please indicate your preference on the application form.

Our School

At The Oxford Academy, we offer pride, aspiration, and opportunity to every member of our community, with significantly improved learning outcomes. We are committed to ensuring that our students and staff are highly successful through sustainable, positive improvements in our school.

Do you want to work in a school that:

  • Is friendly and community-centred, where staff genuinely feel part of a team?

  • Utilises a new teaching approach that has "helped to dramatically improve both pupils' behaviour and participation in lessons. As a result, lessons are undisturbed, and pupils enjoy their learning" (Ofsted 2026).

  • Places staff well-being at the heart of everything we do.

  • Employs a full-time Instructional Coach who works with staff to develop practice through specific teaching goals that maximise student learning.

  • Benefits from a culture where "behaviour across the school is now very positive. Pupils are calm and respectful, with positive attitudes to learning" (Ofsted 2026).

  • Prioritises high-quality bespoke CPLD, supporting staff to gain formal qualifications and apprenticeships via the RLT Apprenticeship Levy and providing collaboration opportunities across a successful and highly respected multi-academy trust.

Community and Connection

The Oxford Academy is an important part of our local community, and we actively encourage individuals from our area—including parents of our students and residents in our neighborhood—to join our team. We believe that being part of a community goes far beyond our physical location; it is about fostering genuine connections, understanding, and mutual support. By investing in local talent, we ensure that our school's values align closely with the daily needs and aspirations of the families we serve.

Many of our team members have deep local roots, including staff who attended the school themselves and have worked here for decades:

‘I have worked at The Oxford Academy for 26 years, having also attended this school as a pupil when it was Peers. Being part of creating successful futures for so many students is something I will always be proud of’ (Long-serving TOA Staff Member).

At our school, we want everyone to feel safe, valued, and respected—not just in theory, but in practice. We are fully committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels they truly belong. Our community deeply embraces its unique character; as noted by inspectors, "pupils are proud of the school's very diverse character, and they appreciate the way they are taught about respect and positive behaviour" (Ofsted 2026). This intentional focus ensures that "pupils are happy in school. They feel known and liked by their teachers. This helps to build the school's sense of cohesion and belonging" (Ofsted 2026).

When you join us, you are not just becoming part of our internal school family; you are joining an organisation that actively cares for and remains a pillar of the local community. We would love to hear from applicants from all diverse backgrounds who share this profound commitment to inclusion.

Employee Benefits

Health & Wellbeing

  • Free annual flu vaccines

  • Discounted gym memberships (onsite gym)

  • Access to an Employee Assistance Programme

  • 24-hour access to a free counselling helpline (including family and debt advice)

  • Flexible working solutions

  • Reduced teaching time

  • Onsite nursery provision through Little Peeple Nursery

Financial

  • Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS), with employee contributions of 19.2%

  • Eligible for a Blue Light Card - Hundreds of offers/discounts on local and national stores

  • Cycle to Work Scheme

  • The Oxford Academy sits outside the ring road and is less affected than other schools by the new Oxford Congestion Charge

Career Progression

  • Opportunities for CPLD and access to apprenticeships

  • Developmental performance management conversations

  • Apprenticeship opportunities for ‘on the job training’

  • Investment in your career, internal and external talent solutions

The River Learning Trust

At RLT, we believe we achieve more together than alone. Our schools are united by shared principles, collaboration, and a belief in the power of education to change lives.

Our Vision: for our schools and SCITT to improve rapidly, continuously, and sustainably — to be better faster together.

Our ‘Why’: children and young people only get one go at school — we aim to ensure it’s the best possible one.

Our ‘How’: through the highest support and challenge for each other, underpinned by shared principles.

Employees benefit from extensive continuing professional learning, strong wellbeing and staff networks, and access to Defined Benefit Pension Schemes (TPS and LGPS). For more information, see our “Working in RLT” guide.

Safeguarding and Recruitment

The River Learning Trust and The Oxford Academy are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all children and preventing extremism. The Trust is required to conduct a variety of checks and online searches about you as part of their recruitment process in accordance with Keeping Children Safe in Education guidance. It is an offence to apply for certain roles within schools if you are barred from engaging in regulated activity relevant to children.

For all RLT Safer Recruitment Documentation candidates should click on the following link RLT Safer Recruitment Documents for Candidates. Please see our website for up to date policies including our Child Protection and Behaviour Policies.

This post is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 and the amendments to the Exceptions Order 1975, 2013 and 2020. For further guidance for applicants click on this link List of offences that are not filtered

Next Steps

We encourage interested candidates to visit the school before applying. To arrange a visit, please contact Reception: enquiries@theoxfordacademy.org . For more information about The Oxford Academy, please visit our website.

title: Executive Assurance Partner
description:
As we embark on the next phase of delivering our ambitious five-year strategic plan, Nexus Multi Academy Trust is seeking an exceptional and experienced school leader to join our central team as an Executive Assurance Partner.

This is an exciting opportunity to influence improvement at scale across a diverse and values-driven Trust, helping to shape the future of education for children and young people with SEND. We are looking for a leader who combines a strong track record of school improvement with curiosity, creativity and a relentless commitment to continuous learning.

Reporting to the Executive Director of Quality Assurance and Improvement, the successful candidate will work collaboratively with Headteachers, Executive Leaders and Trust colleagues to provide high-quality support, challenge and assurance across our family of schools. Through evidence-informed practice, professional dialogue and robust evaluation, you will help ensure that our quality assurance and improvement framework delivers meaningful impact on leadership, governance, staff wellbeing, pupil experience and outcomes.

We are seeking an individual who not only understands what effective education looks like today, but who is also actively horizon-scanning to identify emerging research, innovation and best practice that will shape the provision of tomorrow. You will be confident in translating educational evidence into practical, sustainable improvement strategies and will play a key role in driving innovation across the Trust.

Applicants will have a proven track record of securing sustainable improvements in educational quality and outcomes. You will be a reflective system leader who is energised by collaboration, committed to professional growth and passionate about helping others succeed.

At Nexus, our vision is simple: "Learning together, to be the best we can be." We are therefore looking for a leader whose approach reflects our values of partnership, integrity and continuous improvement. The successful candidate will understand the power of servant leadership, embrace appreciative enquiry, and be motivated by developing people and systems rather than directing them.

This is not a term-time-only position, offering the flexibility of annual leave arrangements and agile working opportunities.

The post will be paid in accordance with the School Teachers' Pay and Conditions Document on Leadership Scale L18-L21 and includes membership of the Teachers' Pension Scheme (unless the appointee chooses to opt out).

title: Information Governance Coordinator
description:
We are seeking to appoint an exceptional Information Governance Coordinator to join our multi-academy trust (MAT) and support our Business Services team through the next phase of growth in Leeds, Bradford, Greater Manchester and Liverpool.

The ideal candidate will:

  • Have experience in a busy administrative, governance or compliance-focused role
  • Be highly organised with exceptional attention to detail
  • Understand the importance of confidentiality, data protection and handling sensitive information appropriately
  • Be able to interpret information, follow established processes and exercise sound judgement
  • Build positive working relationships and communicate clearly with a range of stakeholders
  • Take ownership of their workload and work effectively to deadlines
  • Have a strong moral purpose and drive for continuous improvement

Why choose Dixons Academies Trust?

Our mission is to challenge educational and social disadvantage in the North. title: Deployment Strategist, Internship - Warp Speed
description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


What We're About
 
At its core, the Deployment Strategist role centers around using data in operational and real-world action. Our customers come to us with a hunch that the only way to protect their troops, manufacture high-quality products, structure effective healthcare policies, or deliver aid to refugees safely is to make better use of their data. Deployment Strategists are responsible for turning that hunch into reality.
 
The Role
 
Warp Speed builds on years of excellence in manufacturing to resurrect & revitalize the American Industrial Base. The Warp Speed Deployment role centers around using data in operational and real-world action. Our customers come to us with a hunch that the only way to manufacture high-quality products is to make better use of their data. Deployment Strategists are responsible for turning that hunch into a reality.
 
As a Deployment Strategist, you'll work as part of a driven and creative team of Engineers, Product Designers, and other Deployment Strategists to deploy software against the most exciting problems our world faces. Your mission is to synthesize disconnected streams of thought into an understanding of what the most important problem is, what the data means, what the product needs, what users are motivated by, and where the impact could be.
 
You'll immerse yourself in our customers' most intricate workflows. You'll partner with customer teams and explore the data, and plunge into the product landscape to enable us to scale. A select number of Deployments Strategists may also be deployed to Palantir internal teams and problems. In this role, the problems you'll seek will require a curious and analytical approach, a sharp intuition for product, and a strong degree of user insight to ultimately empower our customers to improve decisions.

title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer, Internship - Warp Speed
description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
Warp Speed
Warp Speed builds on years of excellence in manufacturing to resurrect & revitalize the American Industrial Base. FDSEs on Warp Speed work directly with customers from the factory floor to the board room to understand their greatest problems and design and implement solutions using data.
 
As Forward Deployed Software Engineers (FDSEs) you’ll apply your problem solving ability, creativity, and technical skills to help organizations use their data to drive a real impact in the world. You’ll have the opportunity to gain rare insight into and contribute to some of the most important industries and institutions globally!
 
The Original Forward Deployed Software Engineer 
At Palantir, the Forward Deployed Software Engineer (FDSE) role isn’t just a job title: it’s the blueprint. We pioneered this unique position, embedding talented engineers directly with our customers to tackle their most pressing challenges head-on. As an FDSE, you’ll be at the intersection of world-changing problems and impactful technology, shaping solutions where they matter most.
 
FDSEs work side by side with our customers, rapidly understanding their toughest issues; architecting and building solutions that leverage business-critical data and the latest advancements in AI to solve them. Whether it’s “How do we predict and mitigate wildfire risks to optimize power grids?” or “How can we analyze and adapt a global food supply chain to deliver life-saving aid on time?”, you’ll use your technical expertise, creativity, and problem-solving skills to drive real-world impact.
 
You’ll have the rare opportunity to gain deep insight into and directly influence some of the world’s most critical industries and institutions. By building on Palantir’s powerful platforms leveraging integrated cutting-edge AI, you’ll help organizations unlock the full potential of their data to make smarter, faster decisions.
 
Core Responsibilities
 
As an FDSE, you’ll experience the autonomy of a startup, with the resources, mentorship, and stability of an established tech company. Your contributions will have a direct impact on our customers’ missions and the real world. You’ll work in small, agile teams and own the end-to-end execution and implementation of high-stakes projects, including:
 
• Collaborating with fellow engineers on architecture and design decisions
• Wrangling massive-scale data and using AI to accelerate and enhance critical operations
• Developing custom applications tailored to customer needs
• Engaging directly with customer stakeholders, from technical teams to executives
• Shaping team strategy and driving projects from ideation to deployment, increasing your pain threshold to deliver real value

title: Waiter/ Waitress - Electric House, West London
description:
The Role… 

At Soho House, a Waiter plays an essential role in delivering refined, attentive, and personalised service to our members and guests. Working closely with the floor and kitchen teams, you are responsible for ensuring a smooth dining experience while reflecting the Club’s standards of professionalism, discretion, and excellence.  

Your main responsibility is to ensure that members have an enjoyable experience. You will deliver excellent service from initial greeting, taking orders, making recommendations and paying of the bill. 

What's in it for you?

  • Weekly Pay
  • Team meal whilst on shift prepared by our chefs
  • Soho Friends Membership
  • 50% Team discount on Food & Drink, 7 days a week
  • Staff Room Rates
  • Health Cash Plan (option to up to 2 additional dependents)
  • Dental Plan (option to add up to 2 additional dependents)
  • Birthday Day Off after 1 years' continuous service
  • Up to 50% Staff Discount on Cowshed & Soho Home
  • In conjunction with Soho Impact, take 2 days paid a year to support a charity of your choice.
  • Free Counselling Sessions
  • Cookhouse & House Tonic: Our Cookhouse & Tonic Programmes offer unique food and drink training, events and opportunities to inspire and educate.
  • Continuous training to develop yourself personally and professionally
  • Team Events: From fitness sessions to cinema screenings and art classes, each month we hold a series of fun events which you can sign up to.

Soho House offers competitive compensation packages that feature global benefits and perks. Whether you’re seeking entry-level employment or a new opportunity to expand your profession, we offer training to develop the technical and managerial skills necessary to enhance your career

Key duties…

  • Warmly greet members, introduce menus, and ensure immediate engagement upon seating.
  • Take accurate food and drink orders, accommodating any allergies or dietary needs.
  • Deliver a seamless service by coordinating with kitchen and bar staff, ensuring timely and correct order delivery.
  • Provide knowledgeable recommendations on menu items, including food and drink pairings.
  • Maintain exceptional table service—top up water, wine, and beverages proactively throughout the member’s stay.
  • Ensure a pristine environment, including setting up and resetting tables, and maintaining cleanliness at all times.
  • Handle member requests and special accommodations with flexibility to create memorable, personalized experiences.
  • Support seamless payment through card, the Soho House App, or House Pay.
  • Uphold discretion and professionalism, especially when serving VIPs and PWKs.
  • Contribute to team success, attending briefings, tastings, and assisting colleagues where needed.

 

What we are looking for...

  • 2–3 years in a similar high-end dining environment. 
  • Thrive in fast-paced, high-volume environments and maintain calm, through quickly and effectively problem solving under pressure
  • Must be hospitable, approachable, passionate about customer service and respectful towards colleagues and guests
  • Must be able to demonstrate competency as outlined in the training schedule and Club School
  • Must be able to work flexible shifts and schedules, including weekends and holidays as needed
  • Ability to take direction, work in a team environment and autonomously

title: Analytics Engineer II, Full Stack (Revenue Analytics)
description:
Headquarters: Remote Poland

 At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

 We’re looking for a curious, driven professional to join our Revenue Analytics team. This builds and owns the data products, reporting infrastructure, semantic foundations, and analytical systems that power Affirm’s Revenue organization.
As a Senior Analyst, Revenue Analytics, you’ll build scalable data products that power day-to-day decision-making - owning end-to-end work across data modeling, metric definitions, dashboards, automation, and enablement.
You’ll also help strengthen our semantic layer and data governance, laying the foundation for reliable AI. The ideal candidate combines strong technical and analytical skills with the ability to turn ambiguous business questions into durable, well-tested data infrastructure.

 What you'll do

•
 Develop dbt data models, dashboards, metrics, and automation processes for the revenue field team and revenue analysts

•
 Build and maintain critical reporting data models that power external merchant reporting

•
 Build the semantic, metadata, and context layers that allow AI systems to accurately understand Revenue data, metrics, and business definitions

•
 Partner with Business Systems, engineering, and business stakeholders to translate requirements into durable, well-tested data products

•
 Contribute to the team’s best practices in version control, code review, documentation, and release hygiene (GitHub-based workflows)

•
 Develop processes, governance, and foundations to scale the impact of analytics within Revenue.

 What we look for

•
 3+ years of work experience in an analytics engineering or business intelligence role

•
 Strong working knowledge of SQL, dbt, Python, data modeling, and data visualization

•
 Hands-on experience with BI tools (Sigma/Looker/Tableau), Databricks, and cloud data warehouses (Snowflake)

•
 Understanding of the data foundations required for reliable AI, including semantic layers, metadata, evals, metric definitions, documentation, and data quality

•
 Demonstrated experience integrating AI tools into day-to-day analytics engineering workflows to improve development speed, quality, and scalability

•
 Familiarity with Salesforce and experience supporting commercial areas of the business

•
 Ability to identify user needs and translate them into robust, scalable data products

•
 Ability to start with an ambiguous problem, deconstruct it into tangible steps, and work toward an impactful solution

•
 Ability to communicate findings and recommendations clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

 Total rewards

 We believe the people building honest financial products at Affirm should share in its success. That's why our total rewards are designed to support your health, growth, financial well-being, and future.

 In service of our mission, we reward employees through a combination of base pay, equity (from parent company), and comprehensive benefits.

 Base Pay Grade - K
 226 000 zł - 346 000 zł

 Base pay ranges and placement within those ranges are determined based on several factors, including role, experience, and job-related skills.

 In addition to base pay, all employees in this role are eligible to receive equity from the parent company each year. This means as Affirm’s parent company grows, employees have the opportunity to share in that growth financially.

 Equity Grade - 2 (awarded in US Dollars)

 Affirm Holdings, Inc. Equity Grade example

 Equity grade: 2

 Reward equity: $0-$75,000

 Affirm also provides flexible spending wallets to all employees for technology and wellbeing related needs, which are reimbursable up to 1390 zł per month.

 In addition to your compensation, our comprehensive benefits are designed to support you and the people who matter most. Benefits include:

• Competitive paid time off, paid public holidays, and additional paid Away Days to rest and recharge.

• Comprehensive private healthcare through Lux Med's Platinum package.

• A MultiSport card to support your health and well-being.

• Learning and development programs to help you grow professionally.

• Family healthcare support through Maven and parental leave support through Parentaly.

• Mental well-being support through Lyra, including up to 12 confidential counseling or coaching sessions each year for you and your household members.

• Financial well-being support through Northstar, with unlimited access to Certified Financial Advisors and planning tools at no cost to you.

• Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that foster connection and inclusion.

• Eligibility for creative tax benefits, subject to applicable law, role, and company policy.

 The majority of our roles can be located anywhere in Poland.

 **This job description is not a contractual document, and is not intended to have binding force.**

 Remote-first with flexibility built in
 Affirm is proud to be a remote-first company. Most roles can be done from almost anywhere within the country of employment. Some positions may occasionally require in-person work at an Affirm office, and a few are office-based due to the nature of the work. All new hires will be invited to attend an in-person onboarding experience.

 Benefits designed for you
 Our benefits reflect our commitment to care, transparency, and flexibility. Here are a few highlights:

title: Creative Director - Brand Narrative
description:
Headquarters: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States

 In 1977, Charles and Ray Eames began a film with a picnic beside Chicago’s lakefront. Over the next nine minutes, Powers of Ten traveled out toward distant galaxies and back into the microscopic world inside a human hand. An enormous subject became a journey you could follow, built around a simple change in perspective. Images, language, movement, and sound brought the idea to life together.

 That’s the kind of creative thinking we’re looking for at Mercury: finding a compelling idea inside something complex, then bringing together the people and crafts that make it unforgettable.

 We’re looking for a Creative Director to build and lead Brand Narrative , a new team within Brand Creative. You’ll turn company strategy, product truths, customer insight, and cultural observations into original concepts for our most important launches, campaigns, and brand moments. You’ll originate ideas yourself and stay closely involved as they become finished work.

 Your background might be in art direction, design, or copywriting. What matters is your ability to develop exceptional concepts, recognize the best idea wherever it comes from, and bring the whole creative studio together to make it real. Whatever your starting discipline, you’ll bring deep experience in film-led storytelling.

 You’ll lead Brand Narrative in close creative partnership with your peers leading Brand Design and Writing. Together, you’ll shape concepts, language, and visual expression from the beginning, bringing distinct perspectives and shared ownership to the work. You’ll contribute strong ideas of your own, invite others to challenge and improve them, and build on theirs. This is a role for someone who enjoys making work together, not developing ideas in isolation and handing them off.

 You’ll also shape what Brand Narrative becomes. That means building its culture, developing its people, and establishing ways of working that make the entire studio more creatively ambitious. The opportunity is to make great work while building a team that can keep making it.

 What you’ll do

 In your first year, your focus will be roughly 70% leading creative development for our highest-priority launches and campaigns, and 30% building the Brand Narrative function.

• Originate and lead big creative ideas. Partner with Product Marketing and Brand Marketing on the brief, then turn the agreed audience, opportunity, and product proof into original creative concepts. Develop ideas that can take distinctive forms across film, social, out-of-home, digital, experiences, and partnerships.

• Bring ambitious concepts to life with your creative peers and the full studio. Work side by side with the Brand Design and Writing leads and their teams from the earliest explorations through delivery. Develop ideas together, exchange thoughtful critique, and make creative choices that draw on each discipline’s expertise. Stay hands-on, contribute through your own craft, and partner closely with Motion and Production throughout. For film, remain closely involved through scripts, visual development, production, and the final edit.

• Build audience and distribution thinking into the idea. Shape concepts around how people will discover, watch, and share the work. Work with marketing partners to consider channels and viewing contexts from the beginning, so the work belongs where people encounter it rather than simply being resized to fit.

• Push beyond the first good answer, and learn quickly. Lead thoughtful concept development and critique. Use rough scripts, prototypes, and AI tools to test ideas quickly, learn, and move the strongest work forward. Know when to keep exploring and when to commit, then protect what makes an idea interesting through feedback and production.

• Find opportunities before a brief arrives. Bring curiosity about Mercury’s products, customers, and the wider world. Develop proactive ideas and cultural opportunities that give the brand something meaningful to say or do.

• Help decide where creative ambition matters most. Partner early with Product Marketing, Brand Marketing, Product Design, Comms, and Insights. Help identify which moments deserve our largest creative investment, present recommendations to senior leadership, and use results from marketing and insights partners to inform what comes next.

• Build and lead Brand Narrative. Define the team’s purpose, priorities, creative standards, and ways of working. Help hire and develop the team, shaping its structure and capabilities. Set clear expectations, and coach people to grow their judgment and conceptual strength.

• Create a culture where the best idea wins. Make room for experimentation, honest feedback, and contributions across disciplines. Lead with generosity and conviction, share ownership of the work, and help people challenge one another without making creativity a competition for credit.

• Build practices that strengthen the work. Establish a clear path from insight and an agreed brief to concept and execution, with useful critique and close collaboration throughout. Develop relationships with external creatives and agencies who can add a distinctive perspective or capability when needed.

 What you’ll bring

• A strong creative foundation in art direction, design, or copywriting. Your portfolio shows original concepts developed into ambitious, well-crafted work across multiple formats. You can explain what you contributed, how the idea evolved, and how collaboration made it better.

• Deep film experience. You’ve developed film-led ideas from concept through production, with strong instincts for story, scripts, performance, pacing, and sound. You understand how these choices work together to make an audience feel something, not just make a film look good.

• A track record of deep creative collaboration with design and writing peers. You’ve led ambitious multidisciplinary work from concept through production by building trusted partnerships. You bring a clear point of view, listen closely, work through creative disagreements constructively, and recognize when someone else’s approach makes the work stronger. You can show how your collaborators shaped the outcome, not just what you personally originated.

• Strong taste, cultural awareness, and product curiosity. You can get close to a complex business or product, find the human truth within it, and turn that understanding into something clear, surprising, and memorable.

• Experience developing creative people and shaping how a team works. You give specific, useful feedback, set a high bar with care, and create an environment where people can take creative risks. You’re excited to build a new function, including the everyday practices that give it a culture.

• Clear communication and sound judgment. You can rally people around an ambitious concept, explain why it deserves investment, and navigate competing perspectives without losing the idea. You take ownership in ambiguous situations and balance creative ambition with the need to move work forward.

 What success looks like

 A year in, you’ll have led major launches and film-led campaigns from original concept through finished work, with Brand Design and Writing as creative partners from the beginning. The studio’s disciplines will have shaped the work together, with audience and distribution informing the creative approach.

 Brand Narrative will have a clear identity, shared creative standards, and working practices that help people test and develop stronger ideas together. Alongside planned launches, you’ll have established a pipeline of proactive opportunities that gives Mercury more ways to express its product ambition with originality and cultural relevance.

 Please include a portfolio featuring film-led work and broader campaign concepts. We’d love to understand your role in developing the ideas, the choices you made through production, and how you brought the work to life with others.

title: Law Enforcement Liaison, Kansas
description:
Headquarters: Remote

 Every day, tens of millions of people come to Roblox to explore, create, play, learn, and connect with friends in 3D immersive digital experiences– all created by our global community of developers and creators.

 At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device. We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.

 A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.

 As a Law Enforcement Liaison (Kansas), you’ll develop and advance strategic law enforcement and safety relationships with special focus on law enforcement, while also supporting internal platform safety efforts that elevate the Roblox safety ecosystem. The ideal candidate will be a versatile, self-driven, team-player who enjoys context-switching across high-profile initiatives, and is uniquely motivated by Roblox’s mission of connecting a billion people with optimism and civility. From serving as an external representative of Roblox with state and local law enforcement agencies, to collaborating cross-functionally with our Legal & Advocacy, Civility, Safety, Product, and Communications teams (among others), you will have a diverse set of responsibilities in furtherance of assisting law enforcement, educating external stakeholders such as parents and educators on digital safety, and ultimately helping keep users safe on Roblox.

 This position is remotely based in Kansas and will report to the Senior Manager of US Public Policy.

 Please note: This role requires On-Call support during weekends and holidays, and is expected to include frequent travel. The scope may also require reviewing graphic, controversial, and offensive content in accordance with Roblox’s handling policies.

 You Will:

• Develop and advance strategic law enforcement relationships with special focus on law enforcement in the State of Kansas, and Midwestern region, while assisting with global outreach as needed.

• Coordinate with federal, state, and local law enforcement, including with the Kansas Attorney General’s Office

• Plan and execute educational programs for law enforcement agencies and other key external stakeholders (i.e. parent groups and educators) regarding Roblox’s platform safety efforts, including our law enforcement response policies and NCMEC CyberTip initiatives.

• Proactively identify, monitor, analyze, and internally advise on law enforcement developments affecting Roblox in the State of Kansas and Midwestern region.

• Seek to understand and empathetically respond to regional law enforcement concerns, while helping internally codify and scale resultant learnings.

• Listen to and understand the concerns of Kansas parents, caregivers, and educators regarding the safety of Roblox. You will provide guidance and education that empower these audiences and build confidence in Roblox’s emphasis on product and policy safety, which keeps users safe and healthy.

• Forge a deep subject-matter expertise of Roblox’s internal and external safety practices, so as to identify, advocate for, and help implement strategic safety enhancements.

• Draft professional work product – for both internal and external audiences – supported by clear, concise, and multi-sourced platform safety investigations.

• Collaborate and build strong internal relationships across our Legal & Advocacy, Safety, Product, and Communications teams (among others) to help address law enforcement emergencies, platform safety escalations, and comprehensive Roblox undertakings.

 You Have:

• 10+ years of work experience in law enforcement, intelligence, government, trust and safety, or an adjacent field.

• Detailed knowledge of the law enforcement community and related policymakers in the State of Kansas, and Midwestern region, along with current trends and challenges in online safety and policy (particularly child safety and regional-specific considerations).

• Enthusiasm for and a demonstrated track record of stellar public speaking, short-notice travel, building and maintaining constructive relationships, defining your own work processes, and adding organizational value no matter how small or large the task.

• Outstanding communication, leadership, and stakeholder management skills.

• Agility to navigate ambiguity, resilience to overcome obstacles, and the internal drive to concurrently manage multiple high-profile, time-sensitive initiatives in a dynamic environment.

• Unwavering integrity, collegiality, and grit.

 Roles that are based in an office are onsite Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday, with optional presence on Monday and Friday (unless otherwise noted).

title: Senior Marketing Operations Manager
description:
Headquarters: Remote

 About the Team

 Netlify is a product-led growth company, and Revenue Operations owns the systems, data, and infrastructure that turn that growth into revenue. With a large volume of people discovering and signing up for Netlify every day, Marketing Operations is critical to understanding those users, connecting activity across our systems, and creating scalable ways to engage them throughout their journey.

 As Senior Marketing Operations Manager, you’ll own the operational foundation behind that work. You’ll connect HubSpot, Salesforce, product data, and analytics, build the systems and lifecycle infrastructure that turn signals into action, and give Marketing and our GTM partners trusted visibility into performance. Reporting to the Senior Director of Revenue Operations, you’ll translate the Marketing Operations vision into a roadmap and independently drive it forward while partnering closely with Growth, RevOps, Data, Product, and other GTM teams.

 What You’ll Do

• Execute on the Marketing Operations roadmap, translating broader Marketing and GTM priorities into scalable systems, processes, and programs.

• Own our marketing automation platform end to end, including workflows, lifecycle stages, segmentation, forms, lists, email operations, data hygiene, deliverability, governance, and documentation.

• Build and maintain the connection between marketing automation, Salesforce, product data, and analytics so we can understand and engage users throughout the customer journey.

• Establish reliable attribution and measurement across marketing and product-led journeys, including UTM governance and connections between campaigns, signups, activation, conversion, and revenue.

• Build reporting and self-service dashboards that give Marketing and GTM partners a trusted view of performance and support weekly, monthly, and executive-level decision-making.

• Partner with Growth to operationalize lifecycle programs across email, in-product experiences, and sales-assist triggers, turning customer and product signals into scalable journeys from signup through activation and conversion.

• Build experimentation infrastructure that allows marketers to launch, measure, and learn from tests without requiring engineering support for every experiment.

• Own the operational health of the MarTech stack, including integrations, data flows, governance, vendor relationships, and periodic assessments of what we should keep, retire, consolidate, or integrate.

• Establish scalable practices for high-volume email operations, including audience management, domain and inbox health, deliverability, and safeguards that protect the customer experience.

• Turn large and sometimes ambiguous datasets into actionable recommendations, identifying points of friction or drop-off and partnering with Marketing, Growth, Product, Data, and RevOps on opportunities to improve conversion.

• Own the Marketing Operations portion of the broader Marketing budget and evaluate technology investments based on business value, scalability, and ROI.

• Explore emerging capabilities in AI-enabled marketing operations and AI visibility measurement, helping the team establish useful workflows and baselines as the space develops.

 What You’ll Bring

• 7+ years of experience in Marketing Operations or a closely related discipline, with experience operating independently in a complex B2B SaaS or product-led growth environment.

• Deep experience with marketing automation platforms and CRM systems such as HubSpot, Marketo, Eloqua, and Salesforce, including lifecycle stages, campaign architecture, attribution, lead or account routing, and data governance.

• Experience working with high-volume customer or prospect datasets and designing segmentation, lifecycle, and operational approaches that remain reliable at scale.

• Significant experience operating high-volume email programs, with a practical understanding of deliverability, domain and inbox reputation, audience management, warming strategies, and the risks that emerge at large sending volumes.

• Strong analytical skills and the ability to investigate complex datasets, identify meaningful patterns, question the quality of the underlying data, and turn findings into recommendations.

• Experience building or operating lifecycle, nurture, or in-product engagement programs tied to measurable activation or conversion outcomes.

• Systems thinking and experience designing integrations across marketing automation, CRM, product, analytics, and data systems.

• Experience building measurement and experimentation infrastructure that enables other teams to operate and learn independently.

• Strong GTM fluency and an understanding of how Marketing Operations, Growth, Sales, RevOps, Product, and Customer Success connect to customer experience and revenue.

• Comfort using AI-enabled tools and workflows to accelerate your work while applying judgment to validate outputs and determine where automation is (and isn’t) appropriate.

• Familiarity with product analytics tools such as Amplitude and experience with emerging AEO or AI-visibility tooling is helpful.

• Experience working with contractors, agencies, or distributed partners is helpful but not required.

• Familiarity with developer tools, web platforms, or another high-volume PLG business is useful, but we value relevant operating experience over category-specific expertise.

 This Role Is a Great Fit If

• You enjoy building the foundation, not just operating what someone else has already built. You’re energized by taking an imperfect system and creating something scalable, measurable, and trusted.

• You’re comfortable moving between architecture and execution. You can define how a system should work and then get into the details yourself when necessary to make it work.

• You thrive with significant autonomy. Given a goal and context, you investigate the problem, weigh tradeoffs, make a recommendation, and drive the work forward without needing a detailed playbook.

• You genuinely enjoy data. Large, messy datasets make you curious, and you’re willing to dig until you understand what is happening and what the business should do about it.

• You care deeply about operational quality. Data integrity, attribution, documentation, audience segmentation, and email deliverability aren’t afterthoughts—they’re part of building a trustworthy growth engine.

• You balance speed with judgment. You know when to move quickly, when a shortcut creates unacceptable downstream risk, and when to challenge an approach that won’t scale.

• You see AI as a way to amplify good judgment and increase leverage rather than a substitute for understanding the work.

• You communicate clearly in an async, distributed environment and can build alignment across Marketing, Growth, Product, Sales, RevOps, and Data without relying on organizational authority.

 Applying

 Not sure you meet 100% of our qualifications? Please apply anyway!

 When applying please include:

 A resume or short listing of your job history & skills (link to a LinkedIn profile would be fine). We appreciate a cover letter explaining why you would enjoy working in this role at Netlify to get to know you a bit better, though this is not required and will not impact your application. Our mission is to “build a better web” and that cannot be done without a diversity of skill sets, backgrounds and thoughts.

 Of everything we've ever built at Netlify, we are most proud of our team. Netlify is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are devoted to building a team of people with diverse backgrounds and lifestyles. Driving equality empowers our team, enables us to innovate, and helps us maintain a more inclusive environment. We don’t discriminate against employees or applicants based on gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, race, military/veteran status, citizenship, pregnancy status, or any other differences. If we can do anything to provide a better interview, i.e. accommodate a disability, then please let us know by emailing accommodations@netlify.com .

 About Netlify

 Netlify is the most popular way to build, deploy, and scale modern web applications, empowering everyone from fast moving solo developers to enterprise teams. Millions of developers and organizations rely on Netlify as their platform of choice for composing web applications that are production ready, performant, and flexible. Now, as we embrace the next era of software development, we are embedding the same fluid, intuitive experience into the Agent Experience (AX), making it just as simple for intelligent agents to understand, interact with, and act on our platform as it is for developers. Whether your user is human or machine, Netlify ensures the path from idea to URL is seamless, fast, and deeply reliable.

 We are a Series D company that has raised over $200M from investors such as Andreessen Horowitz, Kleiner Perkins, EQT, Bessemer, BOND, and Menlo Ventures. As a fully distributed company, we aim to create a company culture where the best idea can come from anywhere and strive to be thoughtful, compassionate, and collaborative in our work. If this sounds like something you’d like to be part of, we’re excited to connect with you!

 At Netlify, we are committed to a compensation philosophy that prioritizes fairness and equity, positions our employee compensation competitively in the market, recognizes and rewards performance, and takes a comprehensive approach to our rewards package. We anchor our compensation philosophy on a market-based approach, therefore salary ranges may differ depending on the labor cost in a particular location. The salary provided is in addition to robust benefits and participation in Netlify’s equity plan. Our hiring range for this role is targeted at $155,000 - $210,000 for most US-based locations. Candidates outside the US or in premium markets should consult with their Talent Acquisition partner regarding location-based ranges, as they may be higher or lower than the average US range listed. The starting pay will be determined based on multiple factors, including expertise and skills, market demands, experience, internal equity, and applicable geographic location. These compensation packages and ranges are subject to change and may be modified in the future.

title: Marketing Automation Manager - Canada, Spain, India
description:
Headquarters: Remote

 Storyblok is a headless CMS that enables marketers and developers to create with joy and publish with confidence. It empowers you to deliver structured and consistent content everywhere: websites, apps, AI search, and beyond.

 Legendary brands like Virgin Media O2, Oatly, and TomTom use Storyblok to make a bigger, faster market impact.

 WHAT IS IN IT FOR YOU

 You will be joining a growing company where you can contribute to many “firsts”. Plus these benefits:

• Monthly remote work stipend (home internet costs, electricity). Home office equipment package right at the start (laptop, keyboard, monitor…)

• Home office equipment upgrade (furniture, ear plugs …) or membership to a local co-working space after your onboarding

• Sick leave benefit, parental leave and 25 days of annual leave plus your local national holidays

• Personal development fund for courses, books, conferences, and material

• The annual international team-building trip, quarterly and monthly online get-togethers

• As a fully remote company, with work-life balance at its core, you’ll enjoy flexible schedules

• An international team that loves to have fun at work and works hard together to accomplish shared goals

 JOB SUMMARY

 Storyblok is hiring a Marketing Automation Manager to own the top of funnel systems and the campaigns that run through them: Pardot, the forms on the Storyblok website, list uploads, Clay, and the nurture programs, sequences and webinar flows built in Pardot. The role sends the campaigns, loads the lists and builds the forms day to day, and turns that repeat work into templates and automations so more of the week goes to lead scoring, routing, data quality and reporting. Sitting within Revenue Operations, this role works across Demand Generation, Events, Content, Partner Marketing, Sales Development, Sales Operations and Analytics, in a lean data team where the person pulls their own numbers and builds their own reports.

 ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

• Campaign operations

• Build and send list emails and sequences in Pardot and Knak: webinar invites and follow ups, quarterly enterprise and marketer sequences, review asks, partner and event emails.

• Build and run the nurture programs in Engagement Studio (welcome, post webinar, gated content, re-engagement), each by segment and lifecycle stage, and rebuild them as results come in.

• Set up webinars end to end: registration form, Zuddl to Pardot sync, campaign IDs, reminders and follow up. Build form handlers, autoresponders and landing page forms on the Storyblok website.

• Load lead lists from events, content syndication and paid social with the right campaign, source and consent, and run the request board: intake, SLA, QA before launch.

• Run optimization: Test subject lines, send times and content on every sequence, and personalise by segment, industry and stage.

• Marketing systems and integrations

• Administer Pardot and its Salesforce sync: users, connectors, field mapping, campaign member status.

• Own the links between Pardot, Salesforce, the website, Zuddl, Knak, Meta and Google Ads, and keep them documented.

• Run Clay: enrichment waterfalls, list building, and the signal tables that feed BDR routing.

• Evaluate, buy and renew the marketing tools.

• Lead flow, scoring and routing operations

• Own lead scoring and grading, reviewed each quarter against what converts.

• Own lifecycle stages (MQL, SAL, SQL) and the handoff rules to BDRs and AEs.

• Bring self serve signups and product usage into scoring and lifecycle, so PLG and enterprise leads run through 1 flow.

• Data quality and reporting

• Own the sync between the warehouse, Pardot and Salesforce in both directions: enrichment and usage in, campaign results out.

• Keep the database clean: dedupe, normalise country, industry and title, suppression lists, GDPR consent by region.

• Own the campaign taxonomy and UTM standard across the team and agencies.

• Write your own SQL and Salesforce reports; build the funnel and pipeline by source reports in the BI tool. Watch deliverability: domain health, bounce and spam rates.

• Automation, process and cadence

• Template the repeat request types (list uploads, list emails, form handlers, webinar setups), then automate them with Clay, LLM tools (Claude) and a workflow builder such as n8n or Zapier, each with QA and a fallback.

• Write the playbooks and train marketers to self serve where it is safe.

• Own and report monthly on speed to lead, MQL to SQL and form to meeting rates, request turnaround and share automated, database coverage and accuracy, and email deliverability and engagement.

 EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

• Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business, Information Systems or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

• 4+ years in marketing operations or marketing automation, ideally in B2B SaaS.

• Pardot administration: Salesforce connector, Engagement Studio, form handlers, campaign sync. Salesforce fluency: campaigns, lead and contact fields, reports and dashboards.

• Built nurture programs and can show what they did to conversion.

• Ran a request queue at volume and cut the time per request with templates and automation; shipped automations with a workflow builder and LLM tools and kept them running.

• Lead scoring, lifecycle and routing experience, with results.

• Working SQL, and hands on with an enrichment tool such as Clay, ZoomInfo or Apollo.

• Knowledge of GDPR and consent management across regions.

• Demonstrates AI literacy, with the ability to leverage AI tools to enhance productivity, decision-making, and quality of work while applying sound judgment and critical thinking.

 PROFESSIONAL COMPETENCIES

• Operating discipline: runs a high volume request queue on an SLA with QA before every launch.

• Systems thinking: sees how Pardot, Salesforce, the website, Clay and the warehouse connect, and keeps the data flowing cleanly between them.

• Data fluency: pulls own numbers, defines fields and builds reports without an analyst in between.

• Automation mindset: templates repeat work, then builds the automation that removes it.

• Attention to detail: a wrong list or a broken form reaches thousands of people.

• Testing habit: runs tests on every sequence and changes the program based on results.

• Cross-functional coordination: aligns Demand Gen, Events, Content, Partner Marketing, Sales Development and Sales Ops around 1 lead flow.

• Communication: writes clear playbooks and guidance that marketers follow without a meeting.

 At Storyblok, we are committed to equitable compensation and pay transparency. We consider many factors when it comes to compensation, such as the scope of the role, job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Our base salary ranges are determined by job and job level and are benchmarked to relevant location and industry data. The range displayed represents the target US base compensation range within which we are hiring for this role. For some roles Storyblok also offers a competitive commission structure.

description:
We are recruiting for a Class Teacher in Reception

Required for January 2027

Salary: Teachers Main Pay Range

Hours: Full time / Permanent

St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School, Stourbridge is a happy caring and highly regarded school rooted in Gospel values where pupils are nurtured, educated and experience a true sense of belonging. We maintain the highest expectations for every individual child, carefully developing their talents and self-belief. With a strong Catholic ethos and a warm family feel, we work in partnership with parents and parish to enable every child to flourish academically, spiritually and personally.

If you meet the requirements of the job description and person specification and feel that you could make a positive difference to our school, then we can’t wait to receive your application.

We warmly welcome visits to the school. For specific questions about the role and/or to request a visit, please contact the school office on

Online - www.emmausmac.com

title: Admissions and School Liaison Coordinator
company: Norwich City College of Further and Higher Education
description:
re you passionate about delivering excellent customer service and helping young people take the next step in their educational journey?

City College Norwich is seeking an enthusiastic, organised and proactive Admissions and School Liaison Coordinator to play a key role in supporting prospective students from their first enquiry through to enrolment. This is an exciting opportunity for a customer-focused professional who enjoys building relationships, managing processes and contributing to student recruitment success.

About the Role

As an Admissions and School Liaison Coordinator, you will coordinate admissions activities and support school engagement initiatives across the College. Working closely with prospective students, parents/carers, partner schools and internal colleagues, you will ensure a seamless and positive experience throughout the recruitment and admissions cycle.

You will be responsible for managing applications, interviews, offers and enrolment processes while maintaining accurate student records and admissions data. The role also involves supporting recruitment events, school visits, presentations and engagement activities that encourage applications and support enrolment targets.

As an ambassador for City College Norwich, you will develop strong relationships with schools, careers professionals and other external stakeholders, helping to promote the wide range of opportunities available to our students.

What We're Looking For

Essential

  • Qualified to at least Level 3 (A-Level equivalent).
  • Experience in an administrative role delivering excellent customer service.
  • Experience working with complex databases and information systems.
  • Ability to work effectively within a fast-paced environment and meet deadlines.
  • Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
  • Advanced Microsoft Office skills, including Outlook, Teams, Word and Excel.
  • Excellent communication skills with the confidence to deliver presentations to groups.
  • Ability to work independently while contributing positively to a team environment.
  • Full UK driving licence and access to business insurance.
  • Flexibility to undertake occasional evening and weekend work

Why Join City College Norwich?

At City College Norwich, you'll join a supportive and collaborative team dedicated to transforming lives through education. You'll have the opportunity to make a real impact on students' futures while developing your own skills and career within one of the region's leading educational institutions.

title: Advanced Practitioner (inclusion)
company: Norwich City College of Further and Higher Education
description:
We are seeking passionate, innovative and values-driven practitioners to join our Teaching, Learning and Assessment team as Advanced Practitioners (Inclusion).

These roles have been created through the Inclusive Mainstream Fund (IMF) and represent a significant investment in strengthening inclusive practice across the college. As a result, these positions are offered on a fixed-term basis for three years.

As part of our ambitious commitment to ensuring that every learner can achieve, belong and thrive, Advanced Practitioner’s will play a key role in developing the confidence, capability and effectiveness of teaching staff in meeting the needs of learners with SEND, neurodiverse learners and those facing additional barriers to learning.

Working in partnership with curriculum teams, managers and support staff, you will provide specialist coaching, mentoring and professional development that strengthens inclusive teaching practice, promotes high-quality adaptive teaching, and helps ensure that all learners can access, participate in and succeed within a mainstream learning environment.

About the Role

The college currently employs Teaching and Learning Coaches who support the development of excellent teaching practice across curriculum areas. The Advanced Practitioner role complements and extends this model through a dedicated focus on inclusion, adaptive teaching and learner support.

The successful candidates will work collaboratively with teachers and curriculum leaders to identify barriers to learning, model effective inclusive strategies, provide developmental coaching, evaluate the impact of interventions on learner engagement and deliver intervention sessions to identified groups of learners. They will contribute to the continuous improvement of teaching, learning and assessment by promoting evidence-informed approaches and supporting the implementation of the college's inclusive teaching and learning strategy.

This is an exciting opportunity for experienced practitioners with a strong understanding of SEND, inclusive pedagogy and effective professional development to influence practice across the organisation and make a lasting difference to the educational experiences and outcomes of our learners.

Why Join Us?

This is an exciting opportunity to play a leading role in shaping inclusion across the college. You will have the chance to influence teaching and learning at scale, work alongside talented colleagues, and make a tangible difference to the lives and outcomes of young people.

If you are passionate about inclusion and believe every learner deserves the opportunity to succeed, we would love to hear from you.

title: Cover Supervisor
description:
Salary: starting at £26,879.07 per annum rising annually to £28,458.83 per annum (Scale 4 inclusive of Outer London Weighting)

Hours: 36 hours per week (7:45am to 3:30pm, Monday to Thursday and 7:45am to 3:15pm, Friday, term-time only plus INSET days

Contract: Permanent

Required as soon as possible

We are seeking to appoint an enthusiastic and highly effective individual to become our Cover Supervisor. This is a great opportunity for a self-motivated individual to join our extremely popular and successful school that is committed to providing the best opportunities to students. The role of Cover Supervisor provides stability and continuity for students whose lessons are affected through short-term teaching staff absence.

The role is ideal for someone who enjoys working with young people and wants to play an integral role in supporting teaching and learning in school.

The successful candidate will provide high-quality cover support for lessons and tutorials across the curriculum and support with various duties throughout the school day, including break and lunchtime supervision. This is an excellent opportunity for anyone looking to gain or develop school-based experience.

The purpose of the role is:

  • to ensure the smooth running of cover lessons in the Learning Computer Centre (LCC) and classrooms
  • to cover the Back on Track (BoT) facility and to supervise internally excluded students
  • to assist the pastoral team with administration work

The successful applicant will:

  • have the highest expectations of students

  • have an enthusiastic and positive approach within and beyond the classroom

  • have the necessary IT skills to undertake pastoral administrative tasks

  • have energy, stamina and a sense of humour

Why work at Ruislip High School?

  • Students and staff treat each other with respect. They share high aspirations which are realised through high expectations of everyone.

  • Staff have a range of opportunities to collaborate and develop their career within the Vanguard Learning Trust.

  • Staff are afforded many benefits and rewards as part of the Vanguard Learning Trust’s entitlement package for staff.

  • There are excellent transport links with central London, Buckinghamshire, Hertfordshire and Berkshire.

In joining Ruislip High School you can expect to work in an environment that focuses on teachers improving, rather than proving, their practice; where teaching and learning is at the heart of everything we do; and where all staff work as a community to support our students to fulfil their potential in line with our school’s motto: from grass roots to reaching for the sky.

Applications should be made through My New Term. Information about our school is available on our website: www.ruisliphigh.com.

Please note that we do not accept CVs.

Closing date: 10:00am, Tuesday 10th November 2026

Interview date: to be confirmed

Vanguard Learning Trust is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of its pupils and expects all those working at the Trust to share this commitment. This post is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (Exceptions) Order 1975 (2013, 2020 and 2023). This means that certain convictions and cautions are considered ‘protected’ and do not need to be disclosed to employers, and if they are disclosed, employers cannot take them into account. Guidance about whether a conviction or caution should be disclosed can be found on the Ministry of Justice website (click here).

Vanguard Learning Trust is an equal opportunities employer. We strive to achieve a diverse workforce, fully representative of our community and the wider population in the UK. People of colour and minority ethnic staff are under-represented on our staff body. We are keen to attract applicants from a diverse pool of candidates and are determined to be a great employer for all.

title: School Operations Manager
description:
Job title: School Operations Manager

Location: The King Alfred School, TA9 3EE 

Contract type: Permanent 

Salary: up to £48,738 DOE. 

Salary: includes an element of recruitment and retention allowance

Working hours: 37 per week, all year round


The King Alfred School is looking for a dynamic Operations Manager to join our dedicated team. Reporting directly to the Headteacher, you will act as the vital link and enabler between our school and the Trust Central Team, ensuring our day-to-day operations are seamless, compliant and fully support our vision of a great education for every child.


About the role:

This role is designed to support our Headteacher, working alongside the School Leadership Team to streamline operations and maximise the capacity of school resources. This role will predominantly focus on facilities, compliance and management of the administration function as well as some HR and organisation of school events. This role is an embedded and respected role across the trust, valued by the school and the Senior Leadership Team but there is still an opportunity to make it your own. You will have an eye for detail in relation to systems and operational processes, and will be methodical in your approach to safety and compliance. 

The key aspects of this role are:

  • Building Relationships. It’s vital that you develop and maintain productive working relationships with the Headteacher, Leadership Team, Partnership Team leads and with the school staff. You’ll also be dealing with external contracts.
  • Communication. You’ll need to communicate effectively with all internal and external stakeholders in person, writing, electronically and by telephone. 
  • Compliance. You’ll ensure systems and processes are in place for effective management of essential reporting and contingency plans. You’ll be the first point of contact for facilities, recruitment, and the People team.
  • Operations. Coordination of critical school records will be your responsibility. You’ll act as liaison in relation to staff related safeguarding matters and data protection matters. You’ll manage the site estate team, take responsibility for the admin team and provide support to various school teams as required.


You will be joining us at a really exciting time with the arrival of our new Headteacher in September and the recent merger to form Pathway Trust. To ensure this role is perfectly aligned with our expanding trust and provides the best possible support to the school, the job description will be naturally reviewed and refined in the coming months as our new leadership and structures embed. 

The ideal candidate for this role will be:

  • Highly organised with the ability to manage their time effectively
  • A self starter who is capable of acting on their own initiative
  • Able to influence stakeholders at all levels and demonstrate strong relationship management skills
  • Confident in managing and implementing change
  • An exceptional communicator who is personable and able to build effective working relationships
  • A natural problem solver with the ability to multitask


About us

At The King Alfred School, we are proud to provide a first-class education in a safe, happy and caring environment where every child is supported to reach their full potential. Our Somerset location offers strong transport links, being only two minutes off junction 22 of the M5 and with a train station less than a mile away connected with all major rail links. 

We foster an ethos built on kindness, ambition, resilience and mutual respect, which is reflected in our broad and balanced curriculum and high standards of student conduct. We feature a thriving Sixth Form centre, a dedicated Community Council and student leadership team, the student-led Jill Dando News Centre and a strong track record of active involvement in our local community.

We can offer you: 

  • Happy, engaging students
  • A supportive trust and school community
  • Strong collaboration across the trust family of schools and access to a centralised team of specialists across all areas of school operations
  • A commitment to high‑quality CPD, with dedicated time and budget for your development
  • A values‑driven ethos where diversity, equity and inclusion are lived every day
  • Recognition of continuous service (modification order) to protect employment rights and entitlements
  • Local Government Pension Scheme with generous employer contributions and death‑in‑service cover
  • Access to a fully funded healthcare scheme for all employees and their dependants
  • Occupational sick pay to support you during illness or unexpected emergencies
  • Family‑friendly leave packages to help maintain a healthy work–life balance


In order to apply for this role please complete an application form by 9am, 2nd November. Please let us know if you require any adjustments as part of the process. 

Further details and additional information about our school may be viewed on our website. If you would like to have an informal chat about this role, please contact us to arrange that. 


Please know that depending on the number of applications received we may decide to close the advert early. If you do not hear from us by a week after the closing date then please assume that you have not been shortlisted for an interview. If you have previously applied for this role there is no requirement to apply again, all applications will be reviewed. We wish you all the best in your future and ask that you join our E-Teach Talent Pool so as to keep up to date with all of our latest current opportunities. 


Join us in Providing a Great Education for Every Child

Pathway Trust is committed to equal opportunities and encourages applicants from all backgrounds and communities, as we recognise the importance and benefit this has for our pupils.

title: Chief Information & Technology Officer
description:
We are looking for a corporate leader with substantial professional credibility in information, technology and transformation.

You will bring substantial and current technology expertise, together with experience of applying it at organisational scale. You should be able to move confidently between corporate strategy and the technical substance of a major decision, understanding how choices about infrastructure, platforms, integration and security affect cost, resilience, usability and future capability.

We will expect evidence that you have improved a technology environment that required significant development. You should be able to explain the weaknesses you identified, the choices you made, the alternatives you rejected and the results achieved.

Your previous title will matter less than the scale and quality of your contribution. You may already be a CIO, CTO, CITO, CDIO or equivalent executive. You may have developed the necessary breadth through another senior leadership route.

We are interested in what you have changed, how you achieved it, what endured and what the experience taught you.

Experience in schools or academy trusts is not required.

We actively welcome applicants from other complex sectors, including healthcare, financial services, professional services, retail, logistics, higher education and government.

You will need to demonstrate that you can learn a new context, respect its professional expertise and make sound judgements about which lessons transfer and which require adaptation.

description:
Inspire a Love of Science

Join Millfield’s Science Department

Position: Teacher of Science KS3 and KS4

Full Time: Permanent

Main Scale/UPR: This role is ideal for ECTs and experienced teachers, and we offer a highly supportive induction programme. Start Date: 1st April 2027 or 1st September 2027 Applications Closing Date: 13th November 2026, 9am Interview: 24th November 2026

Are you passionate about working with confident, articulate and ambitious young people?

Millfield is a vibrant, oversubscribed 11 to 16 secondary school with a reputation for excellence in behaviour, attendance, wellbeing and pastoral care. We are looking for an enthusiastic, talented and motivated teacher of science who is committed to delivering outstanding teaching and securing outstanding outcomes for every student.

This is an exciting opportunity to join a dynamic, collaborative and forward‑thinking science department in a school where high expectations, professional growth and a commitment to “Creating Bright Futures” sit at the heart of everything we do.

  • Extra‑curricular opportunities and trips
  • Strong KS3 and KS4 provision with generous curriculum time
  • Classrooms equipped with visualisers to support live modelling

GCSE outcomes have consistently exceeded national averages.

To arrange a visit or an informal conversation, please contact the Headteacher’s PA, Mrs Hall, on 01253 865929 or email admin@millfield.lancs.sch.uk.
