title: Learning Support Assistant
description:
TYPICAL TASKS, DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Curriculum support:

  • Contribute to curriculum planning and evaluation and assist in implementation;
  • Assist in the delivery of lessons/sessions and interact with the teacher and pupils as required; Undertake agreed learning activities/teaching programmes, adjusting activities according to pupil responses;
  • Support and use ICT in learning activities & develop pupils’ competence and independence in its use.

Support for pupils:

  • Support individuals or groups during independent /group work, e.g. explain tasks, reinforce key objectives/concepts or vocabulary, use practical apparatus, support less able pupils, extend/challenge more able, keep pupils on task, interested, motivated and engaged;
  • Occasional support to whole class for short periods.
  • Help pupils to develop communication skills and role play activity;
  • Promote inclusion and acceptance of all pupils, encourage them to interact and work co-operatively and engage in activities;
  • Promote independence and development of self-esteem;
  • Assist in the personal, social, emotional development of pupils and development of self-esteem;
  • Assist with the development and implementation of IEPs/behaviour plans;
  • Use specialist skills/ knowledge/ training to provide support in specialist areas;
  • Encourage and reinforce positive interactions between pupils working within any behaviour targets set; Identify and report uncharacteristic behaviour patterns;
  • Assist with pupil supervision on trips off the premises, under overall guidance of the teacher;
  • Monitor and provide for general care, safety and welfare of pupils, including tasks connected with their social inclusion and personal/physical care.

Support to teacher:

  • Assist with lesson/activity planning, delivery and evaluation;
  • Monitor individual/group achievements of key objectives and provide feedback to the teacher;
  • Contribute to pupil assessment through observation and reporting;
  • Record information relevant to assessment and review of pupils’ progress;
  • Attend IEP and statement review meetings if appropriate;
  • Support implementation of strategies to manage pupil behaviour and help manage pupil behaviour;
  • Active involvement in day to day management of the learning environment including responsibility for the care and preparation of teaching aids, equipment, materials and differentiated resources;
  • Undertake routine and non-routine administrative tasks, e.g. produce worksheets, administer coursework;
  • Liaise with parents/carers, specialist teachers and other professional staff, share and provide information.

QUALIFICATIONS, TRAINING AND LIKELY ABILITIES

  • Ideally educated to degree standard candidates as a minimum will hold a recognised and relevant NVQ level 2 or above qualification and have undertaken other appropriate training (preferably leading to national standards at NVQ level 3) or be able to demonstrate equivalent knowledge, experience and skills.
  • Minimum GCSE (or equivalent) English and Maths at grades A-C
  • Have good communication and listening skills and be able to present information verbally and in writing to others.
  • Have experience of Teaching Assistant work.
  • Have attended further training on aspects of the curriculum or areas of specific special need.
  • Have good level of knowledge and understanding of at least one area of learning (e.g. English, maths, science, etc).
  • Understand school’s policies and how they relate to local and national frameworks/policies (e.g. child protection, health and safety, equal opportunities, SEN).
  • Can use ICT effectively to support learning and use other technology equipment.
  • Can plan own work when required.
  • Can transfer theory/training into practice.
  • Can solve problems and can exercise initiative and independent action.
  • Is pro-active in offering ideas.

Shipston High School is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. This post is subject to an enhanced DBS disclosure.

title: School Business Manager
company: St John Fisher Catholic Comprehensive School
description:
Role Overview

We are seeking an experienced high-calibre School Business Manager (SBM) to provide financial leadership for a highly regarded secondary school in Rochester. You will have operational and strategic responsibility for financial management, human resources, estate management, health and safety, and administrative systems.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide a confidential and professional financial service preparing monthly reports, action plans, and accounts to the Headteacher and Governors.
  • Ensure that all financial reports are completed to a high standard for all auditing purposes and for LA/DfE/Gov returns.
  • Work with external service provider on monthly payroll routines to ensure payments are accurate.
  • Oversee the Purchase Ledger function ensuring all suppliers invoices are paid in a timely manner.
  • Manage external lettings, liaising with external companies seeking to utilise our facilities. Ensure sales invoices are sent and paid in a timely manner.
  • Scrutinise premises, catering, and ICT budgets to ensure best value practices through robust contract and SLA management.
  • Provide strategic oversight on large capital projects and planned maintenance programmes.

  • Proactively identify and secure additional income streams, including grant funding bids and encouraging facility lettings by the local community.

  • Line-manage the Premises Manager and team to deliver the required maintenance, health and safety, and security of our school buildings, facilities and site.

TCAT is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. Learning and Teaching

  • To use Assessment for Learning effectively to assess understanding and inform future planning.

  • To plan and deliver highly effective lessons that challenge all students and ensure that all students make progress.

  • To teach and promote safe working practices, including food hygiene, food safety, personal hygiene and the safe use of catering equipment.

  • To keep up to date with national developments in the teaching of Catering, Food and related subjects.

  • To contribute to the development and delivery of an appropriate, ambitious and high-quality Catering curriculum, including relevant accreditation.

  • To support the delivery of GCSE, BTEC and other relevant qualifications, as required by the school.

  • To develop students' knowledge and understanding of food preparation, cooking techniques, nutrition, menu planning and the principles of professional catering.

  • To provide opportunities for students to develop practical competence, creativity, independence and an understanding of the catering and hospitality industry.

  • To ensure that practical activities are appropriately planned, resourced and supervised, taking account of students' needs and relevant health and safety requirements.

  • Knowledge of National curriculum requirements at KS3 and KS4.

    • Assessment, Monitoring and Reporting

  • To assess and mark students' classwork, practical work and home learning in accordance with the whole-school policy.

  • To maintain accurate records of student attendance, attainment and progress, and monitor classwork and home learning to ensure that it is completed in accordance with the whole-school policy.

  • To report to parents and carers through scheduled parents' evenings and online reporting arrangements.

  • To use assessment information to identify underachievement, inform planning and implement appropriate intervention strategies.

  • To contribute fully to the extracurricular life of the school, including Catering-related activities and events where appropriate.

  • To keep up to date with school information, including the weekly bulletin, staff handbook and relevant school policies.

  • To participate in arrangements within an agreed national framework for the appraisal of your performance.

  • To continue personal and professional development as agreed.

  • To ensure that catering rooms, practical workspaces and equipment are used safely and responsibly, reporting any hazards, faults or maintenance requirements promptly.

  • To ensure that food storage, preparation, handling and disposal are carried out in accordance with relevant food hygiene and safety requirements.

  • To manage practical resources and ingredients responsibly, supporting effective stock control and minimising waste.

  • To contribute to whole-school events as and when required, including Catering-related activities where appropriate.

  • To be aware of the school's duty of care in relation to staff, students and visitors, and to comply with all health and safety policies at all times.

  • To be aware of and comply with the school's codes of conduct, regulations and policies, including its commitment to equal opportunities.

title: Senior / Staff Threat Intelligence Analyst, Hacks
description:
Headquarters: United States

 URL: https://www.trmlabs.com/

 About the Role

 When a protocol is drained, or an exchange is compromised, our customers need to know within minutes or hours which addresses to block and where the funds are going. You will own TRM's answer to that, end-to-end.

 As a Senior / Staff Threat Intelligence Analyst , you will lead TRM's hacks category: the metrics, the system that hits them, and the small contractor team that keeps it running around the clock. We align on the outcome; the approach is yours.

 The impact you will have

•
 Take command when a big hack breaks and act as a leader. Run the response: triage, coordination across teams, internal and customer communications, and the incident report afterwards.

•
 Get every major hack into TRM fast. Make sure every major hack is visible to customers within hours of the first credible public report, around the clock.

•
 Keep TRM's hack data complete and accurate. Every hack, at any size, is recorded with its entity, theft addresses, date, amount, and hack type.

•
 Follow the money at scale. Design the system, with our Data Science and engineering teams, that carries hack-specific attribution downstream as stolen funds move.

•
 Build the machine with AI. Leverage AI to build the tools and agents to automate key parts of hacks analysis and response, while ensuring human quality control over every output.

•
 Explain how it happened. Root-cause the most important hacks and publish best-in-industry technical analysis that makes TRM the first source cited.

•
 See the next one coming. Build approaches that spot vulnerable contracts before they are exploited, and get them into our product.

 What we're looking for

•
 5+ years of professional experience in blockchain intelligence, crypto investigations, cyber threat intelligence, incident response, or a closely related field.

•
 Has owned incident response in a high-stakes environment (exchange, security firm, incident response, or CTI team): war rooms, incident reports, communications under pressure.

•
 Strong blockchain tracing across major chains (BTC, EVM, TRON, Solana), including bridges, cross-chain swaps, and mixers.

•
 Understands how DeFi, bridge, and exchange exploits work, and how attackers behave after the theft.

•
 Applied AI fluency. We expect you to already be building AI-assisted or agentic workflows in your daily analytical work, to be able to show how you validate their outputs and where they fail, and to treat AI as a force multiplier.

•
 Experience managing contractors or leading a small team.

•
 Writes and briefs clearly, from technical deep-dives to executive summaries.

•
 Hands-on and highly accountable: does the hardest work, not only coordinates it.

 Nice to have

•
 Smart-contract reverse-engineering (Solidity).

•
 Experience at a security auditor or blockchain analytics firm.

•
 Experience following specific well-known hacker groups.

 About the Team

 The hacks function sits within TRM's Primary Intelligence organization, alongside the Facilitation & Money Laundering (F&ML) pod. You will work closely with the Nation States, Cyber Threat Intelligence, and Global Investigations teams, as well as with Data Science and Engineering on automation, and with Marketing on publications.

 Team Operating Rhythms

•
 Monthly metrics review with your manager.

•
 Weekly operating sync with your team.

•
 Regular syncs with your team across time zones.

•
 A war room, run by you, whenever a major hack breaks.

•
 On-call responsibilities

 Application Instructions

 If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

 Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

 If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

 Interviewing with TRM

 Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

•
 Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

•
 Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

•
 First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

•
 Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

•
 References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

•
 Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

•
 Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

 Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

 AI Fluency at TRM

 AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

 We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

 At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

•
 Accelerate repeatable workflows

•
 Structure and solve problems

•
 Improve output quality

•
 Increase speed and leverage

 You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

 Life at TRM

 We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

 TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

 Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

 At TRM, you should expect:

•
 Priorities and targets to change quickly

•
 Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

•
 A high level of personal ownership and accountability

•
 Close collaboration across teams and functions

•
 Frequent, high-touch communication

•
 Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

•
 A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

 This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

 We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

 If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

 Leadership Principles

 We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

•
 Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

•
 Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

•
 Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

 Join our Mission

 At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

 TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.

 Privacy Policy and Additional Information

 By submitting your application, you agree to allow TRM Labs to process your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy .

 We collect the information you provide (such as your resume, work history, and contact details) solely for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for current and future roles at TRM.

 Because our hiring cycles for certain positions may span 24 to 36 months, we retain your personal information for up to 36 months from the date of your application. After that period, your data is deleted unless a different retention period is required or permitted by law.

 If you are located in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with applicable data protection laws, you have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal data at any time before that period ends. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at privacy@trmlabs.com .

 To notify TRM Labs that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form (opens in a new tab) . No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

 The use of AI tools of any kind (including but not limited to notetakers, interview assistants, and real-time coaching tools such as Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, Cluey, or similar) during TRM interviews is not permitted without prior approval from TRM. TRM uses its own internal tools for note-taking to ensure a consistent and confidential experience for all candidates.

 We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this form (opens in a new tab) .

 Recruitment agencies

 TRM Labs does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to TRM employees. TRM Labs is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company without a signed agreement.

title: Lead Counsel, Public Company Governance & Corporate Programs
description:
Headquarters: United States

 URL: https://www.hubspot.com/

 Lead Counsel, Public Company Governance & Corporate Programs

 Legal

 Remote - USA

 POS-20140

 The Legal Team

 HubSpot's Legal team is a proactive, business-enabling partner — not a back-office function. We help our teams move fast, smart, and responsibly, balancing innovation with rigor so HubSpot can scale as a publicly traded, AI-native company while maintaining trust, compliance, and clarity.

 Role Summary

 This is a role for a senior governance attorney who has earned the confidence of boards and committees, not just supported them. You will be HubSpot's primary governance lawyer — owning the company's governance policy framework, the NG&S Committee, the operational backbone for all three Board committees, proxy governance and annual meeting, and governance-focused investor engagement.

 The governance attorney who succeeds here doesn't just maintain recurring programs — they actively improve how those programs work, bringing the same rigor to process design as to legal advice.

 HubSpot is building an AI-first legal function, and we want someone who sees that as an opportunity to do governance work at a higher level of quality and scale, not as an obligation to satisfy.

 This is an individual contributor role reporting to the Director of Corporate Legal.

 What You'll Do

 1. Lead HubSpot's Governance Policy Framework

• Own HubSpot's governance policy framework, including committee charters, governance practices, director independence analysis, related-party frameworks, and Board refresh and skills matrix legal analysis.

• Lead the annual governance policy refresh, ensuring HubSpot's practices remain aligned with evolving NYSE requirements and governance best practices — and anticipating changes before they arrive.

 2. Own the Nominating, Governance & Sustainability Committee

• Serve as the substantive legal owner for the NG&S Committee, preparing materials, advising on agenda items, translating legal and governance requirements into practical recommendations, and supporting the committee chair.

• Advise on director independence, related-party considerations, Board refresh, and skills matrix analysis, with the judgment to resolve most questions independently.

 3. Run Board and Committee Operations

• Own the operational backbone for the Board and its Audit, Compensation, and NG&S Committees as a shared service across all three committees.

• Own the governance sections of HubSpot's annual proxy statement, including director biographies, skills matrix, committee descriptions, governance policy disclosures, and ESG and sustainability content, and lead the annual meeting process and logistics end-to-end.

 4. Lead Governance-Focused Investor Engagement

• Lead governance-focused investor engagement, including proxy advisor outreach related to Board composition and governance practices, and partner with Investor Relations on shareholder communications and proxy season strategy.

• Engage directly with ISS, Glass Lewis, and significant shareholders on governance matters with the preparation and credibility to represent HubSpot's positions authoritatively.

 5. Own Corporate Governance Programs

• Own recurring corporate governance programs (governance filings, D&O questionnaires, governance surveys, and related compliance obligations) with disciplined execution and strong records practice.

 6. Build an AI-First Governance Function

• You have a point of view on how AI and automation can raise the quality and efficiency of recurring governance work, and you act on it. You will identify and implement process improvements (including AI-enabled workflows) that reduce friction, strengthen governance operations, and increase the team's operating leverage.

• Build templates, playbooks, and governance infrastructure that make this function more scalable and resilient over time.

 What You'll Bring

 Required Qualifications

• 8-10+ years of corporate and securities law experience at top law firms and/or in-house, with at least 3-4 years of meaningful in-house experience advising a U.S. public company on corporate governance matters.

• Deep knowledge of public company governance (Board and committee practices, director independence, governance policies, stock exchange requirements, and related-party frameworks) with the judgment to own governance calls independently.

• Extensive experience supporting Boards and Board committees, with the credibility to advise on governance matters directly and translate legal requirements into practical, boardroom-ready recommendations.

• Meaningful ownership of, or a senior role in, annual proxy statement preparation and annual shareholder meeting processes.

• Demonstrated track record of governance-related investor and proxy advisor engagement; able to partner with Investor Relations and senior stakeholders as a peer, not a process manager.

• Track record of independently managing complex, recurring governance programs with strong attention to legal judgment, execution, and records discipline — and a drive to continuously improve how those programs run.

• JD from an accredited law school and active bar membership in at least one U.S. jurisdiction.

 Nice-to-Have Qualifications

• Experience working in-house at a publicly traded technology or SaaS company.

• Experience engaging directly with proxy advisors, including ISS and Glass Lewis, on governance matters.

• Experience advising on ESG or sustainability-related governance and public disclosures.

• Hands-on experience using or building AI-enabled workflows in legal or governance contexts, with a clear point of view on where AI adds real leverage in governance work.

description:
Headquarters: USA - Remote

 About Ping Identity:

 At Ping Identity, we believe in making digital experiences both secure and seamless for all users, without compromise. We call this digital freedom. And it's not just something we provide our customers. It's something that inspires our company. People don't come here to join a culture that's built on digital freedom. They come to cultivate it.

 Our intelligent, cloud identity platform lets people shop, work, bank, and interact wherever and however they want. Without friction. Without fear.

 While protecting digital identities is at the core of our technology, protecting individual identities is at the core of our culture. We champion every identity. One of our core values, Respect Individuality, reminds us to celebrate differences so you are empowered to bring your authentic self to work.

 We're headquartered in Denver, Colorado and we have offices and employees around the globe. We serve the largest, most demanding enterprises worldwide, including more than half of the Fortune 100. At Ping Identity, we're changing the way people and businesses think about cybersecurity, digital experiences, and identity and access management.

 We are seeking a strategic and analytical Chief of Staff to partner with our Chief Customer Officer (CCO) in driving business performance across our Customer organization. This role combines financial and operational strategy, data-driven decision-making, and cross-functional collaboration to improve customer retention, revenue performance, and organizational effectiveness.

 The ideal candidate brings strong financial and business acumen, a collaborative mindset, and the ability to translate complex information into actionable insights that inform executive decisions and strengthen financial and operational accountability.

 What You'll Do

• Customer revenue metrics: In partnership with Finance, which owns ARR and financial reporting, to ensure customer metrics (ARR movement, gross and net revenue retention, renewal rates on up for renewal revenue, cohort views and churn drivers) follow Thoma Bravo standards and best-in-class methods. Translates those metrics into the customer organization's view, measures renewal forecast accuracy, and reports on cross-sell and upsell pipeline, which Renewals and Sales own.

• Executive and board narrative: Prepares the CCO's materials for the executive leadership team, board, Thoma Bravo operating reviews and QBRs, framing performance, risk and investment asks in terms of business outcomes. Ensures what the board sees reconciles to how the organization operates.

• Renewal and retention reporting: Owns renewal rate reporting and variance analysis of the official forecast against plan and actuals, explaining the drivers behind the numbers.

• Renewal and retention plan and resource models: In partnership with Finance, builds the customer organization's annual renewal and retention plan (historical baselines, renewal rate assumptions and targets) and the headcount, coverage-ratio and capacity models tied to book-of-business segmentation.

• Customer health and signals: Delivers the customer health scoring model and churn and risk analysis.

• Customer reporting requirements and CCO analysis: Sets the customer organization's reporting requirements across Salesforce, the data warehouse and BI tools, aligned with Finance's metric definitions, which Systems & Operations and Data & Analytics build to. Handles the CCO's own analysis and reporting requests.

• Cross-functional Alignment: Works with Revenue Operations and CRO leadership team to align on strategies and reporting for improving Net Retention Rate. Works with the Product Strategy team to align on churn analysis and forecasting by product.

 What You'll Bring

• Significant experience in strategic finance, FP&A, business operations, revenue operations, customer success operations, or a related field, ideally within a B2B SaaS environment.

• Strong understanding of SaaS business models and recurring revenue metrics, including ARR, GRR, NRR, renewals, and churn.

• Experience translating business needs into reporting and analytics requirements, with familiarity using tools such as Salesforce, Excel, SQL, Power BI, or Tableau.

• Ability to analyze complex datasets and communicate insights clearly to executive audiences.

• Familiarity with CRM, reporting, and business intelligence tools such as Salesforce, Excel, SQL, Power BI, or Tableau.

• Strong collaboration, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to influence across teams.

• Experience in private equity-backed environments or supporting executive and board-level reporting is a plus.

title: Customer Enablement Manager
description:
Headquarters: Remote

 As a Customer Enablement Manager, you will partner with complex enterprise customers to transform how work gets done across their organizations. You will own a portfolio of strategic customers, providing a variety of enablement activities, including discovery, workflow consultation, change management, strategic enablement, and scalable education to accelerate adoption and measurable business outcomes.

 You will work closely with Customer Success, Sales, and Services to understand customer priorities, diagnose barriers to adoption, and recommend strategies that help organizations adopt new workflows and AI-enabled ways of working. As a senior individual contributor, you will serve as a trusted advisor to customers and internal partners, navigate complex stakeholder environments, and help shape repeatable approaches that strengthen Asana's broader Customer Enablement practice.

 This role is West Coast based remote and is open to employees in Pacific or Mountain Standard time.

 What you'll achieve

• Strategic Trusted Advisory: Develop a deep understanding of customer business priorities, operating models, and ways of working. Lead discovery with complex stakeholders and translate customer challenges into clear recommendations for workflow, enablement, and adoption strategies that drive measurable business value.

• Own Complex Customer Engagements: Independently manage complex enterprise engagements within your portfolio of strategic customers, from discovery and planning through delivery, measurement, and follow-through. Navigate ambiguity, competing priorities, and multi-stakeholder environments while keeping engagements aligned to customer and account outcomes.

• Drive Workflow and AI Transformation: Help customers rethink how work gets done by translating Asana and AI capabilities into practical, scalable use cases. Guide customers through the people, process, and behavior change required to successfully adopt new ways of working.

• Executive and High-Impact Facilitation: Design and facilitate workflow consultations, strategic workshops, enablement programs, and executive-level conversations for audiences ranging from end users and champions to senior leaders. Adapt your approach based on customer maturity, organizational complexity, and desired outcomes.

• Measure and Optimize Customer Impact: Use adoption, engagement, and efficacy data to assess whether enablement is driving meaningful behavior change and business outcomes. Identify trends, adjust engagement strategies, and use insights to strengthen customer plans and CEM programs.

• Strengthen Customer Partnerships and Commercial Outcomes: Identify risks, expansion opportunities, and new use cases through your customer engagements. Partner with account teams to connect adoption and enablement strategies to retention, expansion, and long-term customer value.

 About you

• 6+ years of experience in customer enablement, customer success, strategic consulting, implementation, change management, professional services, or a related customer-facing role, ideally within SaaS.

• Demonstrated experience independently leading complex enterprise customer engagements that combine discovery, consultation, facilitation, and enablement to drive adoption, behavior change, or business transformation.

• Strong consultative skills with the ability to uncover root causes, synthesize complex information, challenge assumptions constructively, and translate ambiguity into clear recommendations and action plans.

• Experience engaging and influencing senior and executive stakeholders, including navigating competing priorities and building alignment across diverse stakeholder groups.

• Excellent facilitation and communication skills, with the ability to lead strategic conversations and high-impact sessions for audiences ranging from practitioners to executives.

• Strong project and portfolio management skills, with a track record of independently managing multiple complex customer engagements and driving work forward without significant oversight.

• Strong commercial acumen and an understanding of how adoption, customer value, retention, expansion, and organizational change are connected.

• Strong product and technical curiosity, with the ability to quickly develop expertise in new technology and translate AI and workflow capabilities into meaningful customer use cases.

• Data-informed and outcomes-oriented, with experience using customer signals and metrics to evaluate impact, identify risks, and adjust strategy.

• Proven ability to influence cross-functional partners and contribute to improvements in programs, processes, playbooks, or customer strategy beyond your own individual accounts.

• Comfortable operating in a fast-moving and ambiguous environment, exercising strong judgment, prioritization, and ownership.

• Collaborative teammate who actively mentors others, shares expertise, and helps raise the quality and consistency of the broader team's work.

title: Principal Experience Designer - Visual Design & Design Systems
description:
Headquarters: United States

 URL: https://www.workiva.com/latam/

 Workiva is looking for a Principal Experience Designer to shape the visual future of Unify, our enterprise design system. Unify powers the components, patterns, templates, accessibility standards, and shared experiences used across Workiva’s B2B platform.

 This is a dual-focus principal role. Roughly 60–70% of your time will be spent leading Unify’s visual design direction: evolving its visual language, shaping token architecture, and creating the reference designs and guidance that help teams build consistently. The remaining 30–40% will focus on high-visibility visual work for major conferences, marketing partnerships, and executive audiences. That work is not separate from the system, it’s part of the broader ecosystem of design in which Unify lives.

 You will bring exceptional visual craft, strong systems thinking, and a practical point of view on how design systems need to evolve for AI-assisted design and prototyping.

 What you’ll do

• Define and evolve Unify’s visual language across typography, color, spacing, iconography, motion, and brand expression.

• Partner with the components sub-team and the patterns and templates sub-team to ensure visual design is applied consistently and intentionally across every asset.

• Partner with product design, product mgmt and engineering teams to ensure product experience decisions translate faithfully from system to production.

• Maintain a scalable, semantic token architecture that supports consistent experiences across products and over time.

• Create and maintain a library of reference designs, full-screen examples that demonstrate how Unify should be applied in real product experiences.

• Own visual usage guidance and documentation that make intended use, constraints, and quality standards clear for designers, engineers, and AI-assisted workflows.

• Establish ongoing evaluation of AI-generated designs and prototypes, using what you learn to strengthen tokens, examples, and guidance before inconsistencies reach product teams.

• Lead visual design for select high-stakes moments, including major conferences, executive presentations, product vision work, and marketing partnerships.

• Coach designers and influence cross-functional partners through high-quality feedback, clear principles, and strong visual storytelling.

 What you’ll need

 Minimum Qualifications

• 10+ years of experience in product design, visual design, UX, or related fields, including significant work on platform or enterprise products.

• Bachelor's degree in Design, HCI, or a related field (or 8 years of experience and a Master's degree; or a PhD with 6 years of experience).

 Preferred Qualifications

• A portfolio demonstrating exceptional visual craft and the ability to translate a visual point of view into scalable product systems.

• Hands-on experience with AI-assisted design or prototyping workflows, with a clear perspective on their opportunities and limitations.

• Experience defining or evolving a design system’s visual language, including tokens, components, patterns, and documentation.

• Strong ability to create compelling product narratives for senior leaders and high-visibility audiences.

• Experience partnering closely with engineers and working through the tradeoffs between design intent, system health, and implementation.

• A track record of influencing and coaching teams without relying on formal authority.

• Experience building reference sites, design-system documentation, or machine-readable design guidance.

• Experience with semantic or multi-tier token systems, motion design, presentation design, or event experiences.

• Background in front-end development, developer tools, cross-platform systems, or highly regulated industries.

 Travel Requirements & Working Conditions

• Up to 20-25% travel required to meet with teams, partners, and customers

• Reliable internet connection required for remote or hybrid work environments

 How You’ll Be Rewarded

 ✅ Salary range in the US: $190,000.00 - $315,000.00

 ✅ A discretionary bonus typically paid annually

 ✅ Restricted Stock Units granted at time of hire

 ✅ 401(k) match and comprehensive employee benefits package

 The salary range represents the low and high end of the salary range for this job in the US. Minimums and maximums may vary based on location. The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience and other relevant factors.

 Why Join Workiva

 Workiva is the platform designed to bring confidence, control, and a competitive edge to the world’s most complex organizations. Our AI-powered platform unifies finance, risk, and sustainability on a single, secure foundation—ensuring data is trusted, traceable, and ready to act on. With an unbroken path from source to output, leaders gain confidence in their numbers, visibility into current and emerging risks, and the ability to move with speed and precision in a constantly changing world.

 At Workiva, you’ll bring technology to market that executives, boards, and regulators depend on. The work you do here helps organizations navigate uncertainty, maintain trust, and make decisions that stand up to scrutiny. If you’re energized by meaningful challenges, inspired by collaborative teams, and motivated to help organizations turn uncertainty into advantage, we’d love to meet you.

 Employment decisions are made without regard to age, race, creed, color, religion, sex, national origin, ancestry, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, citizenship status or any other protected characteristic.

 Workiva is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities. To request assistance with the application process, please email talentacquisition@workiva.com .

 Workiva employees are required to undergo comprehensive security and privacy training tailored to their roles, ensuring adherence to company policies and regulatory standards.

 Workiva supports employees in working where they work best - either from an office or remotely from any location within their country of employment.

title: Manager II, Developer Advocacy
description:
Headquarters: California, USA, Remote; New York, USA, Remote; Washington, USA, Remote

 Developer Advocates at Datadog are engineers who share their expertise with technical practitioners, help customers tell their stories, and represent the perspectives of our community inside Datadog.

 As a Manager II on the Advocacy team, you will lead our Community Advocacy functions. You will manage a team of Developer Advocates responsible for global programs such as Datadog Ambassadors, Champions, and User Groups, as well as opportunities for customer engineers to share their expertise through technical writing, public speaking, and other community contributions.

Across these interconnected programs, your team will enable customer engineers to contribute technical knowledge, lead communities, and turn their experiences into compelling content and conference talks for Datadog and third-party channels. This role combines people leadership, program strategy, technical judgment, and cross-functional influence to amplify authentic customer voices, deepen understanding of Datadog and its products, and foster a thriving community of practitioners.

 What You’ll Do:

• Lead and develop a team of Developer Advocates, setting clear expectations, guiding priorities, coaching performance, supporting career growth, and fostering an inclusive, high-performing culture

• Own the strategy, goals, and roadmap for Community Advocacy, translating broader Advocacy and company priorities into focused programs and measurable outcomes

• Guide the continued development of our Ambassador, Champion, and User Group programs, creating clear contributor journeys, expectations, enablement, recognition, and opportunities for customer engineers to increase their impact

• Build repeatable systems that enable customer engineers to contribute technical knowledge, create content, share best practices, and serve as trusted leaders within their communities

• Develop a strong pipeline of customer stories by identifying compelling practitioners and helping them shape authentic, technically credible narratives

• Oversee the support, co-development, and coaching of conference talks by customer engineers—from identifying an idea and developing an abstract through content review, rehearsal, and delivery—for Datadog events, including our flagship user conference, DASH, as well as third-party industry conferences

• Establish measures of success for Community Advocacy, using qualitative and quantitative insights to evaluate program health, contributor engagement, content quality, audience impact, and customer outcomes

• Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, Events, Customer Success, and regional teams to align priorities, identify opportunities, and scale customer participation across Datadog initiatives

• Ensure insights from Ambassadors, Champions, User Group participants, speakers, and other community members are shared with the appropriate teams inside Datadog, strengthening the connection between our customers and our products

• Balance strategic leadership with selective hands-on contribution, including coaching speakers, reviewing technical content, participating in community programs, and representing Datadog when appropriate

 Who You Are:

• You are an experienced people manager who has led autonomous technical professionals, coached performance, developed talent, and translated complex goals into achievable plans

• You have experience defining and delivering successful developer advocacy, developer relations, technical community, or a related functions

• You have built or meaningfully contributed to programs that enable external practitioners to participate, contribute, create content, or lead communities at scale

• You have experience helping technical practitioners develop and communicate their stories, including coaching conference speakers or co-developing technically credible talks and content

• You are a former software developer, SRE, or other technical practitioner—or have equivalent technical depth—with the judgment needed to assess technical accuracy and coach effective technical narratives

• You are a thoughtful cross-functional leader who can build alignment, make prioritization decisions, and influence partners across Product, Engineering, Marketing, Events, and customer-facing organizations

• You use both data and community insight to evaluate program effectiveness, identify opportunities, and make decisions about where the team should invest

• You understand how to build trust with technical communities and value authentic practitioner voices over purely promotional messaging

• You are comfortable operating through ambiguity, establishing structure where needed, and evolving programs as Datadog’s products, customers, and technical audiences grow

 Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply.

 Benefits and Growth:

• New hire stock equity (RSUs) and employee stock purchase plan (ESPP)

• Continuous professional development, product training, and career pathing

• Intradepartmental mentor and buddy program for in-house networking

• An inclusive company culture, ability to join our Community Guilds (Datadog employee resource groups)

• Access to Inclusion Talks, our Internal panel discussions

• Free, global mental health benefits for employees and dependents age 6+

• Competitive global benefits

 Benefits and Growth listed above may vary based on the country of your employment and the nature of your employment with Datadog.

 Datadog offers a competitive salary and equity package, and may include variable compensation. Actual compensation is based on factors such as the candidate's skills, qualifications, and experience. In addition, Datadog offers a wide range of best in class, comprehensive and inclusive employee benefits for this role including healthcare, dental, parental planning, and mental health benefits, a 401(k) plan and match, paid time off, fitness reimbursements, and a discounted employee stock purchase plan.

 Datadog is the leading observability and security platform for the AI era, providing businesses with unified visibility across the technology stack to manage complexity at scale. It brings applications, infrastructure, data, models, and security into one place, using AI to detect and resolve issues before they impact customers. Trusted globally by Fortune 500 companies and high-growth AI leaders, Datadog enables businesses to move faster with clarity and confidence. Learn more about #DatadogLife on Instagram , LinkedIn, and Datadog Learning Center.

title: Senior Customer Engineer - Collibra Public Sector
description:
Headquarters: Remote, USA

 J oining Collibra’s Public Sector team

 The Federal Customer Engineer (CE) serves as the guiding force behind bringing Collibra Public Sector's (CPS) product and vision to customers and prospects. Senior Customer Engineers are responsible for both net-new and expansion opportunities in existing accounts. They establish knowledgeable and trusted relationships from day one and serve as thoughtful technical advisors. The CE maintains a technical relationship with customers throughout the entire customer journey, both pre- and post-sale. You will fill an essential and highly respected role in the sales organization at CPS.

 As a Federal Customer Engineer at Collibra Public Sector, you will support our nation’s most critical agencies in achieving Data Sovereignty and Mission Intelligence . You will partner with Federal Account Executives to navigate the unique procurement and technical landscapes of the DoW, Civilian and the Intelligence Community agencies. Your goal is to show how Collibra’s Self-Hosted and FedRAMP-authorized platforms can break down agency silos, ensure regulatory compliance, and accelerate the secure adoption of AI.

 Senior Customer Engineers at Collibra are responsible for

 Presales

• Lead in-depth technical discovery sessions to uncover complex needs and environments and recommend solutions

• Owns delivery of technical evaluation efforts with input from specialists for (Data Quality, Privacy, AI Governance and the core Collibra Platform).

• Works closely with the Account Executive to craft win-win sales proposals and influence decisions.

• Participates in discovery and drives qualification of new opportunities, and expands Collibra solutions with existing customers.

• Prepares and owns functional and technical sections of RFPs/RFQs.

 Demonstration/Presentation delivery

• Deliver focussed demonstration, creating sample/custom assets and configure workflows as required to meet client needs.

• Deliver focused presentations and roadmaps to key stakeholders across both business and technology

• Deliver complex tailored demonstrations and discuss in detail customization capabilities for specific use cases.

• Present tailored product roadmap presentation based on customer's priorities and current/future use cases

• Deliver complex multi-disciplinary workshops from start to finish involving internal and external stakeholders.

• Lead and own workshops, be the key driver for the agenda, and ensure outcomes result in positive outcomes for client and Collibra.

• Lead product and technical sections of regular business reviews with key customers

• Prepare and conduct product demonstrations, highlighting how Collibra’s Platform can support our Federal Government customer requirements.

• Identifying, evaluating, recommending, and executing value-based workshops and proof of concepts/values.

• Deliver tailored demonstrations that address specific Federal mandates (e.g., OMB M-24-10 regarding AI Governance, CDO Council priorities, and Executive Orders on Data Sharing).

• Lead technical Proof of Value (PoV) engagements within agency environments.

• Ensure successful deployment of Collibra Edge behind agency firewalls.

 Relationship Management

• Acts as the technical authority on Collibra’s security posture, including FedRAMP (Moderate), IL4/IL5 requirements, and SOC2 compliance.

• Acts as a liaison between the client and internal teams on complex requirements and issues that need clarification.

• Leads complex evaluation efforts, coordinating cross-functional resources, and complex testing scenarios.

• Document customer use cases and value realized (or to be realized for new) leveraging value consulting team where relevant.

• Proactively engages with senior-level and strategically important customer/prospect representatives, influencing product-related decisions.

• Develops executive-level credibility and trust, influencing customer-focused solution development and purchasing decisions.

• Build independent relationships to identify growth opportunities.

• Act as a go-to subject matter expert for specific product areas, industries, or complex technical domains.

 Adoption and Expansion

• Architect highly customized and integrated solutions for identified Agency use cases

• Collaborate with Solution Architects in providing guidance on solution design for new use cases.

• Support customer identification of value and ROI. Support customer use case library aligned to data strategy and business value, leveraging the services team when and where required.

• Actively support account growth strategies with the AE/AM.

• Understand in detail the specific differentiators for Collibra solutions, including strengths and weaknesses of competition.

• Provide thought leadership on best practices for adoption and technical optimizations.

• Influences product and service direction to enhance overall client experience.

• Design and validate future-state technical architectures for major transformation projects, integrating across vast complex ecosystems

• Mapping solutions to value across large and dynamic customers, bridging both business and technical requirements.

• Advising and supporting customers’ technical stakeholders to accelerate Collibra adoption and value realization, i.e., be the primary point of contact for technical and product-related queries.

• Architect solutions that function across complex Federal environments, including on-premises, hybrid cloud, and disconnected/classified networks.

• Help agencies build a "Unified Data Language" to facilitate secure data sharing between departments while maintaining strict access controls and data labeling.

 Customer Support

• Address technical questions, mitigate risks, and overcome objections related to security, scalability, integration and implementation.

• Identify adoption roadblocks and ensure successful product usage.

• Drive technical resolution and best practices for common challenges.

• Document customer use cases and adoption challenges, providing guidance on adoption/value realization best practices.

 Teaming

• Provides onboarding assistance for CEs and allied sales team members.

• Contributes to Customer Engineering participation in major projects and provides forward-looking technical guidance.

• Maintain expert-level product knowledge across the portfolio.

• Works internally to improve product marketing messaging and educate Sales/CEs.

• Provides team members with technical and process guidance and advice.

• Build and execute account specific competitive strategies, and contribute to the broader Collibra competitive landscape analysis. Understand the broader technology ecosystem and future trends.

• Packages best practices and lessons learned into thought leadership, methodologies, and published assets to improve Customer Engineering processes.

• Owns Customer Engineering participation in major projects and provides forward-looking technical guidance.

• Supporting sales and marketing activities, webcasts, field enablement, and asset creation.

• Providing advice and feedback to product management and engineering to enhance Collibra solutions and offerings.

 You have

• 5+ years in Sales Engineering or Technical Consulting, specifically supporting U.S. Federal Government customers with 4+ years working in the Data/SaaS space.

• Proficiency in SQL and deep familiarity with Federal data stacks (e.g., Snowflake Government Data Cloud, AWS GovCloud, Azure Government, and Palantir) are a plus.

• Working knowledge of NIST 800-53, FISMA, and the Federal Data Strategy.

• Proven ability to navigate the Federal procurement cycle and build long-term relationships with Agency CDOs, CTOs, and Program Managers.

• Experience should include a broad range of disciplines, including value-based selling, cost-benefit analysis, ROI analysis, process and project management.

• Experience in regulatory compliance and or (financial/IT) audit is a plus.

• Experience working with leading PaaS providers, data lakes, databases, and integration platforms is required.

• Familiarity in enterprise security solutions such as LDAP or Kerberos.

• Experience working with Data Quality, Data Pipelines, Data Orchestration, and/or Job Control tools.

• Knowledgeable of at least least two or three of the following: data management processes, including data governance, data stewardship, master data management, data cataloging, and business rules management

• Experienced with Collibra or comparable technologies

• Demonstrated proficiency in leveraging AI tools (e.g., Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, Copilot) to solve real-world business challenges, drive measurable outcomes, or streamline workflows.

• A bachelor’s degree or equivalent related working experience is required.

• Hold active security clearance (Secret/TS).

• Because this role supports the U.S. government business, it is required that you are a U.S. citizen who resides on U.S. soil.

 You are

• Exceptional in communication, presentation and interpersonal skills including the ability to communicate effectively and build relationships within government entities.

• Fast learner with an aptitude for grasping complex technical concepts.

• Excellent organization and stakeholder management skills.

• A proven collaborator and liaison with all levels and departments within an organization, with experience and success in both partner and contractor-heavy environments.

• Confident in dispensing knowledge to a highly skilled and experienced audience.

• Able to demonstrate a thorough understanding of business needs and revenue potential for accounts in the region.

 Measures of success

• Within your first month, you will become familiar with Collibra Public Sector and understand our customer landscape.

• Within your second month, you should confidently conduct discovery with customers and prospects, initial product demonstrations, and be able to present solutions aligned to customer value.

• Within your third month, you will become a voice for Collibra within your accounts and for your accounts back within Collibra - educating external and internal stakeholders on features, roadmap, and new use cases. Additionally you will drive operational excellence by ensuring the sales process runs smoothly and efficiently.

 Compensation for this role

 The standard base salary range for this position is $140,000 - $175,000 per year. This position is eligible for additional commission-based compensation. Salary offers are based on a combination of factors, including, but not limited to, experience, skills, and location.

 In addition to base salary, we offer a competitive total rewards package, including bonus potential, equity for eligible roles, a Flex Fund monthly stipend, pension/401k plans, and more.
 Benefits at Collibra

 Collibra recognizes and values that everyone has different needs, interests, and life goals. We built our benefits program with flexibility in mind to support you and your loved ones through a diverse range of circumstances and life events. These flexible offerings sit on a foundation of competitive compensation, health coverage, and time off. Learn more about Collibra’s benefits .

 We create inclusion and belonging through how we onboard, meet, connect, engage, and communicate. Learn more about diversity, equity, and inclusion at Collibra.

 At Collibra, we’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We realize the key to creating a company with a world-class culture and employee experience comes from who we hire and creating a workplace that celebrates everyone.

 With this, we proudly consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, pregnancy, sex, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information, physical or mental disability, HIV status, registered domestic partner status, caregiver s

title: Senior Product Designer (Webflow) Temp to Perm
description:
Headquarters: Remote (US)

 Senior Product Designer (Webflow)

 At Current

 At Current, Senior Product Designers (Webflow) lead the design and delivery of engaging digital experiences across multiple client engagements. You'll partner closely with cross-functional teams across strategy, production, engineering, and client services to create thoughtful, user-centered websites that are both beautifully designed and expertly built in Webflow.

 Senior Product Designers are strategic, hands-on creators. You're equally comfortable conducting UX discovery, designing polished experiences in Figma, and building production-ready websites in Webflow. You own projects from concept through launch, partnering with engineering only when advanced custom development or integrations are required.

 What You'll Do

• Lead UX and visual design across websites and digital experiences for multiple client engagements

• Partner with strategy, production, engineering, and client stakeholders to define user experience and creative direction

• Create user flows, wireframes, prototypes, and high-fidelity designs in Figma

• Design and build responsive, production-ready websites directly in Webflow

• Develop scalable design systems, reusable components, and CMS structures in Webflow

• Translate business goals into intuitive, accessible, and conversion-focused digital experiences

• Collaborate with engineers on advanced functionality, integrations, and custom development when needed

• Optimize websites for usability, accessibility, responsiveness, and SEO

• Conduct UX reviews and recommend improvements based on best practices and user insights

• Stay current on UX trends, accessibility standards, and evolving Webflow capabilities

 What You'll Bring

• 5–7 years of UX/UI, Product, or Digital Design experience, ideally within an agency or consulting environment

• 2+ years building production-ready websites in Webflow

• Advanced proficiency with Figma and Webflow

• Strong portfolio demonstrating end-to-end ownership from UX strategy through final Webflow implementation

• Experience building scalable Webflow websites using CMS Collections, Components, and design systems

title: Senior Security Engineer, Detection & Response
description:
Headquarters: U.S. Remote

 About Flexport:

 At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.

 The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

 What you'll do

 There is no MSSP and no tier-1 queue here. Detection & Response engineers own their detections end to end: you write them, you tune them, and your team is paged when they fire. The security team is spread across the globe with a follow-the-sun pager rotation so nobody is paged at 3am local.

 The adversaries are real. The business is growing fast and the threat surface is growing with it. Defining the necessary telemetry is part of the job.

 Detection engineering

• Build and tune detections across endpoint, identity, SaaS, and cloud , treating them as software: version-controlled, peer-reviewed, and shipped through the same CI/CD practices the rest of engineering uses.

• Track detection quality as measured quantities : coverage against MITRE ATT&CK, precision, time-to-detect. We don’t build-and-forget here.

 Response & automation

• Own incident response: triage, contain, remediate, and write the retrospective that turns the incident into a systemic fix.

• Build automation that removes toil from investigations, and partner closely with the US-based team so context carries across time zones instead of getting lost at handoff.

 Telemetry & partnership

• Define telemetry requirements for new systems before they ship , working with infrastructure and product teams to close visibility gaps rather than discovering them during an incident.

• Threat hunt proactively across the estate , converting hypotheses into either new detections or documented coverage.

 You Should Have

• Typically 5–8 years of experience in detection engineering, incident response, or threat hunting, with real hands-on time writing and tuning detections. We care more about what you've built than the exact number.

• Proficiency in at least one programming language (Python, Go, or similar) and comfort writing production-grade detection and automation code.

• Experience with a modern SIEM or detection pipeline (Panther, Elastic, Splunk, or similar). What matters is that you've shipped and tuned detection logic in production.

• Practical incident response experience : you've led or played a major role in triaging and closing out real security incidents.

 Nice to have

• Experience treating detections as code with CI/CD, peer review, and staged rollout.

• Experience defining telemetry contracts for systems before they ship, rather than retrofitting logging after an incident.

• A track record of critically evaluating and verifying AI-assisted work - testing, source-checking, validation - rather than trusting agent output by default. If you haven’t already spotted the em dashes in this job description and already thought about where the hiring manager (hi!) has put hands on keyboard and compared that to where they let the LLM watermarks through, you might not be the right person for the job.

• Familiarity with cloud-native and Kubernetes telemetry.

• Experience with fraud or financial-crime detection patterns.

 How we work

• We stay closely aligned with teammates on other continents via Slack, video, and async docs.

• We have the latest hardware and software, including frontier AI models on day one.

• We're agile, but not dogmatic. Teams decide how they work best.

 Why this role is special

• You own your detections end to end, no MSSP, no tier-1 queue, no handing your work to someone else to triage.

• The consequences here are physical, not abstract: a containment decision can stop a customs filing or freight actually moving, which makes the stakes concrete in a way a SaaS control plane rarely is.

• You'll inherit a real, established estate with legacy telemetry gaps to close, genuinely underexplored surface area, not a well-mined problem.

title: Client Enablement Lead
description:
Headquarters: New York City, Remote

 Alloy is where you belong!

 Alloy is the AI-powered identity and fraud prevention platform that accelerates onboarding, stops fraud, and scales compliance across the customer lifecycle so financial organizations can grow without limits. More than 900 of the world's leading financial institutions and fintechs trust Alloy for smarter risk management that drives growth.

Through our values: Be Bold, Go Fast, Collaborate, and Celebrate Our Differences, we are creating a workplace where you can grow, thrive, and belong. See how we’ve been continuously recognized and named one of Inc. Magazine’s Best Workplaces , Forbes America’s Best Startup Employers , Best Fintech to Work for by American Banker , year after year.

Check out our investors and read more about us here .

 About the team

 Alloy’s platform is complex and managed with high-touch support from Alloy’s Technical Solutions team. Customers that would like to ‘self-serve’ often struggle to build a clear mental model of how Alloy works and why, falling back to Alloy’s support teams to complete even simple tasks. Today, enablement is spread across multiple repositories and handled one-to-one by delivery teams, with inconsistent results. Only a handful of sophisticated and adventurous clients currently achieve a moderate amount of self-sufficiency.

 This leader owns customer enablement across Alloy. This is not a technical writing role. It is a role that builds and runs the program behind enablement: capturing knowledge continuously, packaging it for the right audience at the right moment, running hands-on customer training sessions, and measuring what works.

 The Customer Enablement Lead will report to the VP of Product Design. From within the Product team they will help fill gaps and challenging areas of the product while creating a powerful feedback loop between customers and designers to decrease those gaps and challenges over time. The Enablement Lead will form strong cross-functional connections with the Support, Delivery, Technical Success, Product Marketing, and Product Operations teams to ensure customers have a seamless and supported experience as they go live and as we release new features.

 Alloy operates in a hybrid-work environment. We look to foster collaboration and community by having our local employees onsite three days a week. This role is open to both local and remote candidates in the US.

 What you'll own

 The initial scope of work for this role will include:

 Close Critical Gaps

 Audit the current state. Evaluate and consolidate existing resources (API docs, help articles, the learning center, in-product help, and delivery-built guides). Work with cross-functional partners to create any missing documentation and “Customer 101” program material.

 Outcome : Our AI support bot can answer essentially any customer question. Our delivery teams can pull together the content they need to run tailored training sessions with their customers.

 Deliver the Alloy New Customer Enablement Program

 Focus on new Alloy customers and deliver scalable, deployable training and content for repeatable implementations. Structure material so clients can self-pace from foundational to advanced. Target key user personas so they learn the features critical to their respective day-to-day.

 Outcome : Clients understand and use what they bought, and are aware of what else Alloy offers. Additionally they know where to look for additional guidance via documentation, AI support chat, and other escalation channels.

 Build the Product Release Enablement Program

 When Alloy builds a material new feature or capability, map what each client segment and persona needs to know, when, and why, from pre-sales through go-live and ongoing use, and make it part of how products are sold, launched, and delivered.

 Outcome : a shared view of our friction points and what areas currently drag the most on our bottom line.

 Facilitate the Feedback Loop

 Collect feedback after every release, rollout, and training. Give Product, Design, and Delivery a shared view of where clients get stuck, and drive alignment on whether each gap is best solved by product, technical solutions, or enablement, including interim fixes.

 Outcome : Product, Design, and Delivery share one view of enablement gaps and who owns them. The design team gets critical insight continuously, addressing customer confusion directly in the product, helping reduce the surface area for documentation over time.

 Milestones

 30 Days

 Onboarding into Alloy, learning the product yourself, existing resource audit, gap analysis, start filling documentation gaps with SME and tooling support, and deliver a consolidation plan.

 60 Days

 Initial enablement ‘package’ in beta for first client feedback via early hands-on training sessions.

 90 days

 Initial enablement funnel for core segments deployed and documentation gap filling has demonstrated a measurable increase in AI support ticket resolution. Iteration on the enablement package incorporating early feedback.

 Six Months

 Enablement package is ‘production ready’ and universally rolled out (client-facing teams are ready to deliver training using the material). Feedback loop with product and design solidified. The product release enablement funnel is operational as part of new feature releases. Seeing measurable improvements in some areas of self-service and legacy support ticket theme avoidance.

 Who we’re looking for

 Must-haves:

• 7+ years in customer education, enablement, or training, including building a customer enablement program from the ground up.

• Experience enabling customers on a technical, API-driven B2B SaaS product, with the depth to learn complex workflows and teach them clearly.

• Strong live facilitation. You've run hands-on training sessions with customers and adapted them in the room.

• A track record of tying enablement to measurable outcomes such as ticket deflection, adoption, or time to value.

• Experience influencing Product, Support, Delivery, and Marketing partners without direct authority.

• The judgment to tell when a customer problem needs content, a training, or a product fix, and the writing skills to make the case.

 Nice-to-haves:

• Background in fintech, identity verification, fraud, or compliance.

• Experience structuring knowledge bases for AI support agents or chatbots.

• Hands-on experience with LMS, documentation, or in-product guidance tools.

• Experience working inside a Product or Design organization.
